```text
--
## Design

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Decision | Save this menu's settings in **localStorage**, alongside #116's per-room collaborator directory: one entry per room for hidden collaborators, locked collaborators, the Layering switch and the layer order, plus one global entry for the newcomer default. They're read when a room loads and written when they change, through one small module with a version number. AppState keeps these fields `browser`/`export`/`server` `false`, so they still never reach exports or sync; persistence is handled separately. |
| Alternates Considered | 1. Mark the fields `browser: true` in AppState, so Excalidraw's existing local save stores them. 2. Store them in IndexedDB. |
| Rationale | Alternative 1 saves AppState as one global blob, not per room, so a hidden collaborator in one room would carry into every other room. It also mixes these settings with the scene save, where they're easy to leak into files. Alternative 2 is asynchronous and heavier than needed for a few small lists. A per-room localStorage entry matches how #116 already stores the directory, is synchronous at load, and keeps all this menu's persistence in one place. |
| Consequences | Saved settings can refer to collaborators who never return; they're kept in the room's entry (small) and ignored if unknown. A version number lets later issues add settings without breaking old entries. Hiding my own drawings is deliberately not restored (Criteria I). |

--
author:	CashenCroft
association:	collaborator
edited:	true
status:	none
```

```text
Root cause: `setupTests.ts` sets `EXCALIDRAW_ASSET_PATH = file://${__dirname}/`; on Windows Vite resolves fonts to `/@fs/C:/…`, giving `file:///c:/…/@fs/C:/…` → ENOENT → SVG falls back to font URLs instead of inlined base64.

**How to apply:** to prove a branch matches CI, temporarily patch `fetchFont` in setupTests.ts to read `decodeURIComponent(url.pathname).split("/@fs/")[1]`, run the suite (expect 159/159 with committed snapshots unchanged), then `git checkout -- setupTests.ts`. ```text
```
```text
Ensure Default Behaviors for New Users

# Issue Description

## Summary

Adds a **default for newcomers** and **saved settings** to the collaborator dropdown from #116, #81 and #82.

- **Newcomer default.** A "New collaborators" setting (**Visible / Locked / Hidden**, default **Locked**) decides how a collaborator is treated the first time this client sees them. With the default, newcomers' drawings are visible but can't be selected or edited (#81's visible-only mode) until I unlock them.
- **Newcomers in the layer order.** While layering is on (#82), a newcomer is placed last, **directly above "unknown / miscellaneous"**.
- **Saved settings.** This menu's settings are remembered locally across page reloads: the newcomer default, hidden collaborators, locked collaborators, the Layering switch, and the layer order.

Like the rest of this menu, everything is local to my client. It never changes the shared scene or what other collaborators see.

## User Story

**As a** collaborator in a busy or open room, **I want** people I see for the first time to start visible but locked on my screen, and my visibility, lock and layering choices to be remembered, **so that** newcomers can't be accidentally edited or clutter my view, and I don't have to set everything up again each session.

## User Scenario

A team lead runs a design session in a shared room. Before anyone new arrives, the "New collaborators" setting is already on Locked (the default). When a new student joins and starts drawing, the lead can see the student's work but can't accidentally select or move it. Because layering is on, the student is placed just above Miscellaneous in the layer order. The lead unlocks the student once they've settled in. The next day, the lead reopens the room: the layering order, the hidden and locked collaborators, and the newcomer setting are all as they left them. Nobody else in the room sees any of these settings.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium

**Specific:** Lesser Medium (5 points)

**Reason:** Builds on #116 (collaborator directory, which already records each collaborator the first time they're seen, and is already saved per room), #81 (locking) and #82 (layer order). This issue adds one setting, applies it at the point the directory records a new collaborator, changes where newcomers enter the layer order, and adds a small local persistence layer that saves and restores this menu's settings. It touches no element data, sync, or server code.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Criteria A: Newcomer default setting.** The collaborator dropdown has a "New collaborators" setting with three options: Visible, Locked, Hidden. It defaults to **Locked**.
- [ ] **Criteria B: Applied to first-seen collaborators.** When this client sees a collaborator for the first time (they aren't in the collaborator directory yet), they start in the chosen state: Visible → visible and interactive; Locked → visible but locked; Hidden → hidden (and therefore locked, per #81). A collaborator seen before (in the directory, even if they left) is not affected when they rejoin.
- [ ] **Criteria C: Only future newcomers.** Changing the setting doesn't change any collaborator already seen. The existing Show all / Hide all / Lock all / Unlock all controls still work for them.
- [ ] **Criteria D: Newcomers in the layer order.** While layering is on, a newcomer is added directly above "unknown / miscellaneous" (below every collaborator already in the order). Several newcomers are added in join order. This replaces #82's Criteria H ("added to the bottom").
- [ ] **Criteria E: Me and Miscellaneous.** The setting never applies to me or to the "unknown / miscellaneous" bucket.
- [ ] **Criteria F: Settings are remembered.** After a page reload, the newcomer default, hidden collaborators, locked collaborators, the Layering switch and the layer order are restored as I left them. The newcomer default is one preference for all rooms; the other settings are saved per room, like #116's directory. This replaces the "resets on reload" criteria of #116, #81 (G) and #82 (F).
- [ ] **Criteria G: Local only.** Saved settings stay on this device. They are never synced to other collaborators, included in exported files or shared links, or added to undo/redo history.
- [ ] **Criteria H: Shared-state integrity.** Applying the default or restoring saved settings changes no element (`index` and `version` stay the same) and sends nothing new to other collaborators.
- [ ] **Criteria I: Safe restore.** Saved settings that refer to collaborators no longer known, or that are unreadable or from an older version, are ignored without errors, falling back to the defaults. Hiding my own drawings is not restored on reload, so a room never opens stuck in view mode (#116 forces view mode while my own drawings are hidden).

## Resolved Questions

- **Who is "new"?** Anyone this client sees for the first time, meaning they aren't in #116's collaborator directory yet.
- **Does changing the default affect people already here?** No, only future newcomers (Criteria C).
- **Where do newcomers go in the layer order?** Directly above Miscellaneous (Criteria D).
- **Can the default control what the newcomer sees?** No. Like the rest of #14, it only changes what *I* see on my own screen.

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

- Controlling what other collaborators see, or any server-side permissions.
- Syncing settings between devices or accounts.
- Notifying me when a newcomer joins.
- Per-room newcomer defaults.
- Changes to how ownership, co-ownership (#84) or the layer ordering rule itself work.

## Related

- **Depends on:** #116 (directory, visibility), #81 (locking), #82 (layer order; PR #180, which this issue changes in Criteria D)
- **Design decisions:** see the Design comment below

## Head Issue

Issue (#14): Allow a togglable Layer in which all users are compartmentalized by interactivity and visibility. (#14: "A default for new joining users so that you don't have to see all users.")
```

```text
=================== PR 180
feat(editor): local collaborator layering (#82) [OPEN] feat/issue-82-user-priority-and-layering

Closes #82 (Sub-issue of #14)

## Why

In a busy room, one collaborator's drawing can end up buried under someone else's large shapes. The shared drawing order (`index`) belongs to everyone, so changing it to fix my view would change it for the whole room. #116 lets me hide collaborators and #81 lets me lock them, but neither changes what is drawn on top.

This PR adds **local layering**: I can put collaborators in the order their drawings are layered on _my_ screen, without touching the shared order or what anyone else sees. It follows the [Design comment on #82](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/82): a **Layering** switch in the collaborator dropdown.

- **While it's off,** nothing changes.
- **While it's on,** each row gets **↑ · ↓** controls, and the row order is the layer order: the top row is drawn on top.

It builds on:

- **#116:** ownership via `customData.creatorId`, the rules in `element/ownership.ts`, the dropdown, and the collaborator directory;
- **#81:** the interactivity rule and locking;
- **#84:** co-ownership, which merged into `master` during this work. An element edited by several collaborators has several owners.

Some points the ACs didn't fully specify were settled during implementation and recorded in the [implementation decisions comment on #82](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/82#issuecomment-6998689678):

- the first switch-on order;
- Reset;
- newcomers;
- co-owned elements.
```

```text
28	## What changed
29
30	- **One ordering rule.** `orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer` (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`) is a pure, stable sort by each element's layer: higher rows are drawn on top, each collaborator keeps the shared order, and labels stay with their containers. While layering is off it returns the input unchanged. Co-owned elements (#84) use their highest visible owner's layer. Helpers next to it build the default order (me on top, then join order, miscellaneous last), add newcomers to the bottom, and move rows.
31	- **Used everywhere "what's on top" matters:** canvas rendering (`Renderer.ts`), hit-testing and arrow binding (`App.tsx`, `binding.ts`), and PNG/SVG export (`prepareElementsForRender`), so what's drawn, clicked, bound and exported always agree. The shared `index` is never changed.
32	- **Local state only:** `collaboratorLayeringEnabled` and `collaboratorLayerOrder` in AppState are never saved, exported or synced, and the actions add no undo history.
33	- **UI:** a Layering switch and Reset order in the collaborator dropdown. While layering is on, the rows become one list in layer order with ↑ · drag handle · ↓, on desktop and phone.
34	- **#84 integration:** one line in #84's co-owner stamp notifies the scene while layering is on, because co-owning can move an element to another layer. As intended by the [implementation decisions](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/82#issuecomment-6998689678), a co-owned element can change layer when its owners change.
35	- **Export dialog fix (`445dd32e`):** the dialog's JSON snapshot now keeps the layering Maps, which fixes a freeze when opening Export image with layering on.
36	- **Mutation testing:** see [`82-CashenCroft.md`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/blob/eeb5fc90/docs/sprint3/mutation/82-CashenCroft.md) (86.51% → 87.74%).

286	feat(editor): local collaborator lock / visible-only mode (#81) [MERGED] feat/collaborator-lock

288	Closes #81 (Sub-issue of #14)
289
290	## Why
291
292	In a shared room it's easy to accidentally select, drag, or delete a teammate's drawing while working next to it. #116 let users *hide* collaborators, but hiding removes the drawing you may want to reference. This PR adds a **visible-only (locked)** mode so a collaborator's work stays on screen as a reference but can't be changed from your client, without affecting anyone else.
293
294	This is a **carryover of #80 via #116**: #80 asked for per-collaborator visibility _and_ interactivity controls. #116 delivered visibility (ownership via `customData.creatorId`, the central rule in `element/ownership.ts`, the dropdown). This PR delivers the interactivity half, built on the same structures, following the design decision posted on #81.
295
296	## What changed
297
298	Adds a local, per-collaborator **lock** to the collaborator dropdown. A locked collaborator's drawings stay visible on my screen, but I can't select, move, resize, rotate, delete, erase, or text-edit them. Everything is local to my client: nothing is synced, saved, or exported, and other collaborators notice nothing.
299
300	### The rule (one pure function)
301
302	- `isCollaboratorInteractive` in `packages/element/src/ownership.ts`: **hidden → never interactive** (no interactivity without visibility); **your own bucket → always interactive** (can't be locked); otherwise **locked → not interactive**.
303	- Pure lock-list helpers next to it: `addLockedCollaborators`, `toggleLockedCollaborator` (ignored while hidden or for yourself), `unlockVisibleCollaborators` (hidden collaborators stay locked).
304	- Element-level wrappers `isElementInteractive` / `excludeNonInteractiveElements` (bound text follows its container; never-seen creators and untagged elements follow the miscellaneous bucket, as in #116).
305
306	### State and actions
307
308	- `AppState.lockedCollaboratorIds` (default empty; `browser`/`export`/`server` all `false`, so it's never persisted, exported, or synced and resets on reload).
309	- New actions `toggleCollaboratorLock`, `lockAllCollaborators`, `unlockAllCollaborators`. All use `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` (no history, nothing to sync).
310	- #116's hide actions (per-collaborator toggle and "Hide all") now also lock whoever they hide, so a collaborator who is shown again stays locked until unlocked (Criteria C).
311
312	### Enforcement
313
314	Interaction chokepoints now ask the interactivity rule instead of the visibility-only check: hit testing (click select, double-click text edit, path-target pick), `selectGroupsForSelectedElements` (marquee, lasso, Select All, groups), the App selection safety net (also re-run when the lock list changes), and the eraser. Rendering, export, search, and **arrow binding** stay visibility-only: per the amended Criteria E, arrows may still bind to locked (visible) elements, never to hidden ones. The element's built-in `locked` property is not used (it syncs and would break Criteria F).
315
316	### UI
317
318	Each dropdown row (in the room, previously seen, and "Untagged & unknown") gets a lock toggle beside its visibility toggle: disabled and shown locked while the collaborator is hidden, disabled and shown unlocked on your own row. "Lock all" / "Unlock all" are enabled only when they'd change something (both disabled after "Hide all"). Same component on desktop and in the phone main menu. #116's row button is unchanged (same test id, `aria-pressed`, text), now wrapped next to the lock button.
319
320	### Intended behavior: things attached to my elements still follow them
321
322	The lock blocks direct changes to a locked collaborator's elements. Changes that come from my own elements are kept:
323
324	- **Frames:** dragging my frame moves everything inside it, including locked elements. I own the frame's location, not the positions inside it.
325	- **Bound arrows:** a locked collaborator's arrow bound to my shape still follows my shape (bindings are kept, as in #116).
326	- **Path targets:** dragging my path still moves the elements it targets, like a frame.
327	- **Deleting my frame:** locked children are released where they are (`frameId` cleared), not deleted.
328
329	### Commits
330
331	- `78523efe` state logic · `027e95ef` enforcement · `458e868f` UI · `09013e13` fix: bulk buttons disabled when they'd change nothing (found in manual testing) · `d7e29804` repair mis-encoded characters in test names · `27ab30e7` AI log
332

427	## What changed
428
429	Implemented local client-side visibility controls for collaborators' drawings, ensuring users can independently show or hide individual, all, or none of their peers' drawings without affecting shared scene data, sync status, or other clients' views.
430
431	### Ownership & Identity (`excalidraw-app`)
432	- Implemented a one-time `customData.creatorId` stamp applied by the client that first introduces an element to the room (ensuring edits never transfer ownership, and pastes or duplicates belong to the paster).
433	- Added a robust per-tab client ID system utilizing a `localStorage` pool, Web Locks, and `sessionStorage` to allow reopened tabs to correctly reclaim their ID.
434	- Introduced non-volatile `USER_IDENTITY` messaging on join, new-user creation, and renames, with optional `clientId` support added to pointer and idle payloads while maintaining compatibility with older clients.
435	- Implemented a locally persisted, per-room "previously seen" collaborator directory.
436
437	### Editor & UI Architecture (`packages`)
438	- Extended `AppState` with `hiddenCollaboratorIds`, `collaboratorDirectory`, and `viewModeBeforeSelfHide` (configured to never be persisted, exported, or synced).
439	- Established a single centralized visibility rule (`element/ownership.ts`) consumed across rendering, hit-testing, selection/binding chokepoints, the eraser tool, search, and exports.
440	- Configured hidden elements so they cannot be selected, erased, bound to, or exported (while preserving existing bindings), routing never-seen creators and untagged elements into a shared miscellaneous bucket.
441	- Added toggle, show-all, and hide-all actions, including automatically locking view mode with an explanatory banner when a user hides their own drawings.
442	- Created the collaborator visibility dropdown menu positioned next to the avatars for both desktop and mobile views.
443
444	## Why
445
446	Collaborative sessions can quickly become visually cluttered, making it difficult for users to focus on specific work streams or review individual contributions. Providing client-side visibility controls allows users to filter what they see locally without disrupting the shared state, modifying real-time sync, or interfering with what other collaborators view on their own screens.
447
448	## Tech Debt
449
450	**Introduced:** Added an extra redundant guard at the selection and deletion chokepoints that explicitly validates collaborator visibility before applying destructive scene operations. While strictly redundant with the internal state checks in `element/ownership.ts`, this additional failsafe intentionally compromises pure architectural separation to guarantee that hidden peer elements can never be accidentally selected, mutated, or permanently erased during bulk operations. This can be removed in the future if internal safe-guards are considered enough, or until architectural design is modified in a way to properly encompass a failsafe pathway.
451
452	**Encountered:** None. Implementation of this was built from scratch. Because of this, no test cases existed and had to be made.
453

456	- Added 129 comprehensive feature tests covering multi-client collaboration flows through the real Collab/Portal, complete with control cases and mutation checks.
457	- All existing tests pass, and typecheck, lint, and Prettier checks are clean.
```

```text
  private reportIdle = () => {

  private reportActive = () => {

  private initializeIdleDetector = () => {
    document.addEventListener(EVENT.POINTER_MOVE, this.onPointerMove);
    document.addEventListener(EVENT.VISIBILITY_CHANGE, this.onVisibilityChange);

  setCollaborators(sockets: SocketId[]) {
    const collaborators: InstanceType<typeof Collab>["collaborators"] =
      new Map();
    for (const socketId of sockets) {
      const isCurrentUser = socketId === this.portal.socket?.id;
      collaborators.set(
        socketId,
        Object.assign(
          {},
          this.collaborators.get(socketId),
          { isCurrentUser },
          // lets the editor tell which creator id is "you"
          isCurrentUser && this.clientId ? { id: this.clientId } : {},
        ),
      );
    }
    // collaborators who just left: refresh when we last saw them
    for (const [socketId, collaborator] of this.collaborators) {
      if (!collaborators.has(socketId) && collaborator.id) {
        this.recordSighting(collaborator.id, collaborator.username);
      }
    }
    this.collaborators = collaborators;
    this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
      collaborators,
      appState: { collaboratorDirectory: this.collaboratorDirectory },
    });
  }

  updateCollaborator = (socketId: SocketId, updates: Partial<Collaborator>) => {
    const collaborators = new Map(this.collaborators);
    const user: Mutable<Collaborator> = Object.assign(
      {},
      collaborators.get(socketId),
      updates,
      {
        isCurrentUser: socketId === this.portal.socket?.id,
      },
    );
    collaborators.set(socketId, user);
    this.collaborators = collaborators;

    if (user.id) {
      this.recordSighting(user.id, user.username);
    }

    this.excalidrawAPI.updateScene({
      collaborators,
      appState: { collaboratorDirectory: this.collaboratorDirectory },
    });
  };

  public setLastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion = (version: number) => {

  public getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted = () => {

  public getClientId = () => this.clientId;

   * Records a sighting of `clientId` in the current room's directory, saving
   * it when it changed. Returns whether it changed.

  private recordSighting = (clientId: string, username?: string | null) => {
    if (!this.directoryRoomId) {
      return false;
```

```text
/** a collaborator seen at some point in the current room */
export type CollaboratorDirectoryEntry = Readonly<{
  username: string | null;
  /** epoch ms */
  lastSeen: number;
}>;

export type CollaboratorPointer = {
---
};

/** structurally satisfied by the editor's AppState */
export type CreatorLayering = CreatorVisibility &
  CreatorSelf & {
    /** layering on → elements are drawn in `collaboratorLayerOrder` */
    collaboratorLayeringEnabled?: boolean;
    /**
     * local layer order of visibility buckets, top row (drawn on top) first.
     * `null`/omitted → the default order.
     */
    collaboratorLayerOrder?: readonly string[] | null;
  };

/**
 * The layer order used when layering is first turned on, and on reset (#82):
 * you on top, then everyone in join order, the miscellaneous bucket last.
 *
 * Join order is the order of `collaboratorDirectory` (#116), which records
 * each collaborator the first time this client sees them (a `Map` keeps
 * insertion order). Live collaborators not recorded yet follow it.
 */
export const getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder = (
  state: CreatorVisibility & CreatorSelf,
): string[] => {
  const order = new Set<string>();
  const selfId = getSelfCreatorId(state);
  if (selfId) {
    order.add(selfId);
  }
  for (const id of state.collaboratorDirectory?.keys() ?? []) {
    order.add(id);
  }
  for (const collaborator of state.collaborators?.values() ?? []) {
    if (collaborator.id) {
      order.add(collaborator.id);
    }
  }
  order.add(UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID);
  return [...order];
};

/**
 * The layer order shown in the dropdown and used for drawing (#82): the
 * stored order (or the default one), with anyone not in it yet added to the
 * bottom in join order. Ids are never dropped, so collaborators who are
 * hidden or left keep their place.
 */
export const getCollaboratorLayerOrder = (
  state: CreatorLayering,
): readonly string[] => {
  const defaultOrder = getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder(state);
  const stored = state.collaboratorLayerOrder;
  if (!stored) {
    return defaultOrder;
  }
  const known = new Set(stored);
  const newcomers = defaultOrder.filter((id) => !known.has(id));
  return newcomers.length ? [...stored, ...newcomers] : stored;
};

/**
 * Returns `order` with `id` moved to `toIndex` (clamped to the list), or
 * `order` itself when nothing changes (unknown id, or already there).
 */
export const moveCollaboratorLayer = (
  order: readonly string[],
  id: string,
  toIndex: number,
): readonly string[] => {
  const fromIndex = order.indexOf(id);
  const targetIndex = Math.min(Math.max(toIndex, 0), order.length - 1);
  if (fromIndex === -1 || fromIndex === targetIndex) {
    return order;
  }
  const next = order.filter((other) => other !== id);
  next.splice(targetIndex, 0, id);
  return next;
};

/**
 * The single layering rule (#82), used for rendering, hit-testing, binding
 * and export: while layering is on, elements of a higher collaborator in the
 * layer order are drawn after (above) every element of a lower one. The sort
 * is stable, so each collaborator keeps the shared drawing order. Bound text
 * follows its container's owners. Buckets missing from the order go below
 * everyone.
 *
 * A co-owned element (#84) is drawn in the layer of its highest VISIBLE
 * owner, like it follows its least restricted owner for visibility and
 * locking. If every owner is hidden (it isn't drawn then), its highest owner
 * is used.
 *

 * input array as-is while layering is off.

 * @param elementsMap used to resolve bound text containers. Defaults to a map
 * of `elements`, so pass the full scene map when `elements` is a subset.
 */
export const orderElementsByCollaboratorLayer = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  state: CreatorLayering,
  elementsMap?: ElementsMap,
): readonly T[] => {
  if (!state.collaboratorLayeringEnabled) {
    return elements;
  }

  const rankByBucket = new Map(
    order.map((id, index) => [id, order.length - 1 - index]),

    );
  };
  return elements
    .map((element) => ({ element, rank: getRank(element) }))
    .sort((a, b) => a.rank - b.rank)
    .map(({ element }) => element);
};
```

```text
          }
          disabled={!isLayering}
          data-testid="collaborator-layer-reset"
        >
          {resetIcon}
          {t("collaboratorLayer.resetShort")}
        </button>
      </div>

      {showSearch && (
        <QuickSearch
          placeholder={t("quickSearch.placeholder")}
          onChange={setSearchTerm}
        />
      )}

      {isLayering ? (
                />
              ))}
            </section>
          )}

          {previouslySeen.length > 0 && (
            <section>
              <div className="CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__section-title">
                {t("collaboratorVisibility.previouslySeen")}
              </div>
              {previouslySeen.map((row) => (
                <Row
                  key={row.id}
                  row={row}
                  label={getLabel(row)}
                  hint={t("collaboratorVisibility.leftHint")}
                  onToggle={toggle}
                  onToggleLock={toggleLock}
                />
              ))}
            </section>
          )}

          {/* hidden while filtering by name (it has no name) */}
          {!term && (
            <section>
              <div className="CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__section-title">
                {t("collaboratorVisibility.miscellaneous")}
              </div>
              <Row
                row={rows.miscellaneous}
                label={t("collaboratorVisibility.miscellaneousRow")}
                hint={t("collaboratorVisibility.miscellaneousHint")}
                onToggle={toggle}
                onToggleLock={toggleLock}
                avatarless
              />
            </section>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
};

/**
 * Rounded-square ⋯ button next to the collaborator avatars, opening the
 * local-only drawing visibility controls.
 */
export const CollaboratorVisibilityMenu = ({
  className,
}: {
  className?: string;
}) => {
  const appState = useUIAppState();
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  const hasHidden = appState.hiddenCollaboratorIds.size > 0;

  return (
    <Popover.Root open={isOpen} onOpenChange={setIsOpen}>
      <Popover.Trigger
        className={clsx("CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__trigger", className, {
          "is-active": hasHidden,
        })}
        title={t("collaboratorVisibility.title")}
        aria-label={t("collaboratorVisibility.title")}
        data-testid="collaborator-visibility-trigger"
      >
        {DotsHorizontalIcon}
        {hasHidden && (
          <span
            className="CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__badge"
            data-testid="collaborator-visibility-badge"
          />
        )}
      </Popover.Trigger>
      {isOpen && (
        <Popover.Content
          className="CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__popover"
          align="end"
          sideOffset={10}
          style={{ zIndex: 2 }}
        >
          <Island padding={2}>
            <MenuContent />
          </Island>
        </Popover.Content>
      )}
    </Popover.Root>
  );
};
import clsx from "clsx";

import "./RadioGroup.scss";

export type RadioGroupChoice<T> = {
  value: T;
  label: React.ReactNode;
  ariaLabel?: string;
};

export type RadioGroupProps<T> = {
  choices: RadioGroupChoice<T>[];
  value: T;
  onChange: (value: T) => void;
  name: string;
};

export const RadioGroup = function <T>({
  onChange,
  value,
  choices,
  name,
}: RadioGroupProps<T>) {
  return (
    <div className="RadioGroup">
      {choices.map((choice) => (
        <div
          className={clsx("RadioGroup__choice", {
            active: choice.value === value,
          })}
          key={String(choice.value)}
          title={choice.ariaLabel}
        >
          <input
            name={name}
            type="radio"
            checked={choice.value === value}
            onChange={() => onChange(choice.value)}
            aria-label={choice.ariaLabel}
          />
          {choice.label}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};
```

- **Callers:** `updateCollaborator` ([Collab.tsx:1046-1066](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L1046-L1066)) handles pointer, `USER_IDENTITY` and idle messages from peers. `setCollaborators` ([:1036-1040](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L1036-L1040)) handles people leaving, and `startCollaboration` and `setUsername` record me.

The storage key is `excalidraw-collaborator-directory` ([app_constants.ts:52](excalidraw-app/app_constants.ts#L52)). It keeps 20 rooms and 200 entries per room, and on reload the entries come back newest-first.

- **AppState:** defaults are at [appState.ts:140-145](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L140-L145), and all flags are `false` at [:291-300](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L291-L300). Types are at [types.ts:592-618](packages/excalidraw/types.ts#L592-L618).

That covers hide and show (hiding also locks, :48-60), lock and unlock (:112-256), and the layering switch, move and reset (:169-235). In Collab, `startCollaboration` ([:555](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L555)) and `destroySocketClient` ([:454](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L454)) reset only the hidden set.

Since Miscellaneous is usually the stored bottom row, newcomers land **below** it. Newcomers are computed each time and never written into the stored order.

## 3. Room load and the self-hide view mode

- **Room load:** `startCollaboration` ([Collab.tsx:512](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L512)) is where the directory loads, before the socket opens.
- **Two resets wipe everything:** `resetScene` ([App.tsx:3207-3218](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L3207-L3218)) replaces the **whole AppState** with defaults. Joining an existing room calls it twice: [Collab.tsx:600](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L600) and `initializeRoom` [:803](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L803). The directory survives only because Collab republishes it from memory at [:831/836](excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L831). So the restore has to run **immediately after each reset**, not only at start.
- **Self-hide:** [App.tsx:3826-3846](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L3826-L3846) in `componentDidUpdate` forces view mode whenever `isOwnDrawingsHidden` is true, meaning my id is in the hidden set. ## Risks

- **First-seen with a restored directory:** this is safe. The directory loads synchronously before the socket opens, so everyone already in it counts as returning.
  - Someone pruned from the directory (the 200-per-room cap) counts as new again.
  - My own other tabs have different client ids, so they count as newcomers too. That matches the issue's definition, but it may surprise people.
- **Ids that never return:** they stay in the room entry, which is bounded by the 20-room cap. They are harmless:
  - Their elements already fall into the Miscellaneous bucket.
  - `getCollaboratorLayerRows` skips ids that have no row.
- **Race between restore and resets:** this is the real risk.
  - Joining calls `resetScene` twice, and `onChange` would then **save the empty defaults over the saved settings**.
  - Fix: mark settings as not restored before each reset, and restore synchronously right after it in the same tick, so no socket handler can run in between. Saving is skipped while settings aren't restored.
  - One gap remains: if a newcomer arrives during the async gap before the first `App.initializeScene`, their default is saved to storage but can be overwritten in AppState by the initial-load snapshot. I'll cover it with a test in Phase 4 if the harness can reproduce it.
- **Layer order across reloads:** newcomers are written into the stored order when they first appear, so their order survives a reload. Otherwise the directory's newest-first reload would swap them.
- **Fix that comes with this:** `lockedCollaboratorIds` and layering currently carry over between rooms, because only the hidden set is reset. A per-room restore fixes that.

## Questions

1. **Criteria D when Miscellaneous isn't the bottom row.** The user can move Miscellaneous up, and then "directly above Miscellaneous" and "below every collaborator already in the order" disagree. I recommend following "directly above Miscellaneous" literally.
2. **My own id missing from a restored order.** A tab with a new client id would make me look like a newcomer, so I'd land above Miscellaneous. Criteria E says the setting never applies to me. I recommend putting me on top, as #82's default order does.
3. **"Resets on reload" tests in #81 and #82.** These are `collaboratorLock.test.tsx:316` "AC-G: lock settings reset when the page reloads" and `collaboratorLayer.test.tsx:366` "AC-F: the layer order resets when the page reloads". They still pass, because they check the scene's own local save, which still doesn't store these fields. But their names contradict #83's Criteria F. Should I leave them, or rename only the titles (e.g. "…is not restored by the scene's local save")? Your rule limits test edits to Criteria D.
4. **A pruned collaborator who returns** with leftover saved hidden or locked state. I recommend applying the newcomer default and replacing that leftover state, since by Criteria B's definition they're first-seen.

```text
/** structurally satisfied by the editor's AppState */
export type CreatorInteractivity = CreatorVisibility & {
  /**
   * creator ids locked on this client (visible but non-interactive).
   * `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` locks the miscellaneous bucket.
   */
  lockedCollaboratorIds?: ReadonlySet<string>;
};

/**
 * The interactivity rule (#81): whether this client may interact with a
 * visibility bucket's elements.
 *
 * - hidden → never interactive (no interactivity without visibility)
 * - your own bucket → can't be locked
 * - otherwise → interactive unless locked
 */
export const isCollaboratorInteractive = (
  bucketId: string,
  { hiddenCollaboratorIds, lockedCollaboratorIds }: CreatorInteractivity,
  selfId: string | null,
): boolean => {
  if (hiddenCollaboratorIds?.has(bucketId)) {
    return false;
  }
  if (bucketId === selfId) {
    return true;
  }
  return !lockedCollaboratorIds?.has(bucketId);
};

/** returns the lock list with `ids` added, never including yourself */
export const addLockedCollaborators = (
  lockedCollaboratorIds: ReadonlySet<string> | undefined,
  ids: Iterable<string>,
  selfId: string | null,
): Set<string> => {
  const next = new Set(lockedCollaboratorIds);
  for (const id of ids) {
    if (id !== selfId) {
      next.add(id);
    }
  }
  return next;
};

/**
 * Returns the lock list with `bucketId` toggled. Ignored for hidden buckets
 * (their lock can't change while hidden) and for yourself.
 */
export const toggleLockedCollaborator = (
  state: CreatorInteractivity,
  bucketId: string,
  selfId: string | null,
): Set<string> => {
  const next = new Set(state.lockedCollaboratorIds);
  if (bucketId === selfId || state.hiddenCollaboratorIds?.has(bucketId)) {
    return next;
  }
  if (!next.delete(bucketId)) {
    next.add(bucketId);
  }
  return next;
};

/**
 * Returns the lock list after "unlock all": every visible bucket is
 * unlocked, hidden ones stay locked (so they're still locked once shown).
 */
export const unlockVisibleCollaborators = (
  { hiddenCollaboratorIds }: CreatorInteractivity,
  selfId: string | null,
): Set<string> =>
  addLockedCollaborators(undefined, hiddenCollaboratorIds ?? [], selfId);

/** structurally satisfied by the editor's AppState */
export type CreatorSelf = {
  collaborators?: ReadonlyMap<
    unknown,
    Readonly<{ id?: string; isCurrentUser?: boolean }>
  >;
};

/** this client's creator id (the current user's collaborator entry), if any */
export const getSelfCreatorId = ({
  collaborators,
}: CreatorSelf): string | null => {
  for (const collaborator of collaborators?.values() ?? []) {
    if (collaborator.isCurrentUser && collaborator.id) {
      return collaborator.id;
    }
  }
  return null;
};

/**
 * Whether this client may interact with the element (select, move, resize,
 * rotate, delete, erase, text-edit): when ANY of its visibility buckets is
 * interactive per `isCollaboratorInteractive`, i.e. it follows its least
 * restricted owner. Elements whose buckets are all hidden never are.
 *
 * @param selfId defaults to the current user's id from `state.collaborators`;
 * pass it when checking many elements.
 */
export const isElementInteractive = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
  state: CreatorInteractivity & CreatorSelf,
  selfId: string | null = getSelfCreatorId(state),
): boolean =>
  getElementVisibilityBuckets(
    element,
    elementsMap,
    state.collaboratorDirectory,
  ).some((bucketId) => isCollaboratorInteractive(bucketId, state, selfId));

/**
 * Filters out elements this client may not interact with (hidden or locked
 * collaborators'). Returns the input array as-is when nobody is hidden or
 * locked.
 *
 * @param elementsMap used to resolve bound text containers. Defaults to a map
 * of `elements`, so pass the full scene map when `elements` is a subset.
 */
export const excludeNonInteractiveElements = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  elements: readonly T[],
  state: CreatorInteractivity & CreatorSelf,
  elementsMap?: ElementsMap,
): readonly T[] => {
  if (
    !state.hiddenCollaboratorIds?.size &&
    !state.lockedCollaboratorIds?.size
  ) {
    return elements;
  }
  const map = elementsMap ?? arrayToMap(elements);
  const selfId = getSelfCreatorId(state);
  return elements.filter((element) =>
    isElementInteractive(element, map, state, selfId),
  );
};
```

```typescript
 *
 * - B: a collaborator seen for the first time (not in #116's directory yet)
 *   starts in the chosen state: Visible → visible and interactive; Locked →
 *   visible but locked; Hidden → hidden (and therefore locked, per #81). A
 *   collaborator seen before (in the directory, even if they left) is not
 *   affected when they rejoin
 * - C: changing the setting doesn't change anyone already seen
 * - D: with a layer order, a newcomer is added directly above
 *   "unknown / miscellaneous"; several newcomers in join order
 * - E: never applies to me or to the miscellaneous bucket

 *
 * `getNewcomerState` is given the state from before the sighting is

});

const ALL_DEFAULTS: NewCollaboratorDefault[] = ["visible", "locked", "hidden"];

    // carol is seen first, then dave (with carol now in the directory)
    const afterCarol = { ...first, ...getNewcomerState("carol", first)! };
    const afterDave = getNewcomerState("dave", {
      ...afterCarol,
      collaboratorDirectory: directory("me", "alice", "bob", "carol"),
    })!;
    expect(afterDave.collaboratorLayerOrder).toEqual([
      "me",
      "alice",
      "bob",
      "carol",
      "dave",
      UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
    ]);
  });

  it("AC-D: with miscellaneous moved up, a newcomer still goes directly above it", () => {
    const next = getNewcomerState(
      "carol",
      state("locked", {
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: true,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: ["alice", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID, "me", "bob"],
      }),
    )!;
    expect(next.collaboratorLayerOrder).toEqual([
      "alice",
      "carol",
      UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
      "me",
      "bob",
    ]);
  });

  it("AC-D: a newcomer who joins while layering is off is above miscellaneous once it's turned on", () => {
    const next = getNewcomerState(
      "carol",
      state("locked", {
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: ["bob", "me", "alice", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID],
      }),
    )!;
    expect(next.collaboratorLayerOrder).toEqual([
      "bob",
      "me",
      "alice",
      "carol",
      UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
    ]);
  });

  it("AC-D: before layering was ever turned on, there's still no stored order", () => {
    // #82: the order is null until first turned on; the default order then
    // already lists the directory (join order) above miscellaneous
    const next = getNewcomerState("carol", state("locked"))!;
    expect(next.collaboratorLayerOrder).toBe(null);
  });

  it("AC-D: doesn't mutate the stored order", () => {
    const order = ["me", "alice", "bob", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID];
    getNewcomerState(
      "carol",
      state("locked", {
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: true,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: order,
      }),
    );
    expect(order).toEqual(["me", "alice", "bob", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID]);
  });
});
```

```typescript
/**
 * Issue #83 — the collaborator dropdown's saved settings
 * (`collab/collaboratorSettings.ts`). Expected values come from the
 * acceptance criteria in #83 and its Design comment, not from running the
 * implementation:
 *
 * - F: the newcomer default, hidden collaborators, locked collaborators, the
 *   Layering switch and the layer order are restored as I left them. The
 *   newcomer default is one preference for all rooms; the rest is per room
 * - I: unreadable data or data from an older version is ignored without
 *   errors, falling back to the defaults; hiding my own drawings is never
 *   restored
 * - A: the newcomer default's default is Locked
 * - Design comment: one versioned localStorage entry next to #116's
 *   directory; collaborators who never return are kept (and ignored if
 *   unknown)
 * - defaults otherwise (#116, #81, #82): nobody hidden or locked, layering
 *   off, no stored layer order
 */
import { vi } from "vitest";

import { STORAGE_KEYS } from "../app_constants";
import {
  loadCollaboratorSettings,
  saveCollaboratorSettings,
} from "../collab/collaboratorSettings";

const KEY = STORAGE_KEYS.LOCAL_STORAGE_COLLABORATOR_SETTINGS;

const DEFAULTS = {
  newCollaboratorDefault: "locked",
  hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
  lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
  collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
  collaboratorLayerOrder: null,
};

/** every setting changed from its default */
const CHANGED = {
  newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" as const,
  hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["bob"]),
  lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice", "bob"]),
  collaboratorLayeringEnabled: true,
  collaboratorLayerOrder: ["alice", "me", "bob", "__unknown__"],
};

const readStored = () => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)!);
const writeStored = (value: unknown) =>
  localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(value));

beforeEach(() => {
  localStorage.clear();
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

describe("collaborator settings — Criteria F (remembered)", () => {
  it("AC-F: every setting round-trips as I left it", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(CHANGED);
  });

  it("AC-F: hidden and locked collaborators come back as sets", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    const loaded = loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me");
    expect(loaded.hiddenCollaboratorIds).toBeInstanceOf(Set);
    expect(loaded.lockedCollaboratorIds).toBeInstanceOf(Set);
  });

  it("AC-F: the newcomer default is one preference for all rooms", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      "room-a",
      { ...DEFAULTS, newCollaboratorDefault: "visible" } as any,
      "me",
    );
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-b", "me")).toEqual({
      ...DEFAULTS,
      newCollaboratorDefault: "visible",
    });
  });

  it("AC-F: hidden, locked, the Layering switch and the order are saved per room", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      "room-b",
      {
        ...CHANGED,
        hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["carol"]),
        lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["carol"]),
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: null,
      },
      "me",
    );

    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(CHANGED);
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-b", "me")).toEqual({
      ...CHANGED,
      hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["carol"]),
      lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["carol"]),
      collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
      collaboratorLayerOrder: null,
    });
  });

  it("AC-F: a room's settings don't carry into a room never saved", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-new", "me")).toEqual({
      ...DEFAULTS,
      // the one global preference
      newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
    });
  });

  it("Design: sets are stored as plain arrays in one versioned entry", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    const stored = readStored();
    expect(typeof stored.version).toBe("number");
    expect(JSON.stringify(stored)).toContain('["bob"]');
    expect(JSON.stringify(stored)).toContain('["alice","bob"]');
  });

  it("Design: collaborators who never returned are kept in the room's entry", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      "room-a",
      { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["long-gone"]) },
      "me",
    );
    expect(
      loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me").hiddenCollaboratorIds,
    ).toEqual(new Set(["long-gone"]));
  });

  it("Design: keeps only the 20 most recently used rooms, like #116's directory", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 25; i++) {
      saveCollaboratorSettings(`room-${i}`, CHANGED, "me");
    }
    // the room saved last is always kept, the oldest is dropped
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-24", "me")).toEqual(CHANGED);
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-0", "me")).toEqual({
      ...DEFAULTS,
      newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
    });
  });
});

describe("collaborator settings — Criteria I (safe restore)", () => {
  it("(control) hiding a collaborator other than me is restored", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      "room-a",
      { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]) },
      "me",
    );
    expect(
      loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me").hiddenCollaboratorIds,
    ).toEqual(new Set(["alice"]));
  });

  it("AC-I: hiding my own drawings is not restored", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      "room-a",
      { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["me", "alice"]) },
      "me",
    );
    expect(
      loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me").hiddenCollaboratorIds,
    ).toEqual(new Set(["alice"]));
  });

  it("AC-I: my own id saved as hidden (e.g. saved without knowing me) is dropped on load", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      "room-a",
      { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["me", "alice"]) },
      null,
    );
    expect(
      loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me").hiddenCollaboratorIds,
    ).toEqual(new Set(["alice"]));
  });

  it("AC-I: nothing saved → the defaults (newcomers Locked)", () => {
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
  });

  it("AC-I: unreadable data → the defaults, without throwing", () => {
    localStorage.setItem(KEY, "not json");
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);

    writeStored(["not", "settings"]);
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);

    writeStored(null);
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
  });

  it("AC-I: data from an older version → the defaults", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    const stored = readStored();

    writeStored({ ...stored, version: stored.version - 1 });
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);

    const { version: _version, ...withoutVersion } = stored;
    writeStored(withoutVersion);
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
  });

  it("AC-I: settings with the wrong shape fall back to their defaults", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    const stored = readStored();
    writeStored({
      ...stored,
      newcomerDefault: "purple",
      rooms: {
        "room-a": {
          updated: 1,
          hidden: "bob",
          locked: [1, 2],
          layeringEnabled: "yes",
          layerOrder: { 0: "alice" },
        },
      },
    });
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
  });

  it("AC-I: a broken room list keeps the newcomer default", () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
    writeStored({ ...readStored(), rooms: "broken" });
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual({
      ...DEFAULTS,
      newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
    });
  });

  it("AC-I: saving doesn't throw when storage is unavailable", () => {
    // (the test setup's localStorage is a plain object, so spy on it directly)
    const setItem = vi.spyOn(localStorage, "setItem").mockImplementation(() => {
      throw new Error("quota exceeded");
    });
    expect(() =>
      saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me"),
    ).not.toThrow();
    expect(setItem).toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("AC-I: loading doesn't throw when storage is unavailable", () => {
    vi.spyOn(localStorage, "getItem").mockImplementation(() => {
      throw new Error("blocked");
    });
    expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
  });
});
```

Here are the Phase 2 test cases, file by file. Each test's code is followed by what each part does and where its expected value comes from. Layer orders are listed top row first; drawing orders are listed bottom first.

---

# 1. `ownershipNewcomer.test.ts` (new, 19 tests)

[packages/element/src/**tests**/ownershipNewcomer.test.ts](packages/element/src/__tests__/ownershipNewcomer.test.ts)

### Shared setup

```ts
import {
  UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
  getNewcomerState,
  isCollaboratorInteractive,
} from "../ownership";
import type { NewCollaboratorDefault } from "../ownership";
```

- `getNewcomerState` and `NewCollaboratorDefault` don't exist yet; Phase 3 adds them.
- `isCollaboratorInteractive` is #81's existing rule. The tests use it, so "visible but locked" is judged by the same rule the app uses, not by checking sets directly.

```ts
const directory = (...clientIds: string[]) =>
  new Map(clientIds.map((id) => [id, { username: id, lastSeen: 0 }]));
```

- This builds #116's directory. Map insertion order is the order people were first seen, i.e. join order.
- This helper and `room` below are copied from `ownershipLayer.test.ts`.

```ts
const room = (...clientIds: string[]) =>
  new Map(
    clientIds.map((id, i) => [`${id}-socket`, { id, isCurrentUser: i === 0 }]),
  );
```

- This builds `appState.collaborators`. The first id is me (`isCurrentUser`), which is how #81's `getSelfCreatorId` finds me.

```ts
const state = (newCollaboratorDefault, extra = {}) => ({
  collaborators: room("me", "alice", "carol"),
  collaboratorDirectory: directory("me", "alice", "bob"),
  hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["bob"]),
  lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice", "bob"]),
  collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
  collaboratorLayerOrder: null,
  newCollaboratorDefault,
  ...extra,
});
```

The scenario used by every test:

- **me:** in the room and the directory.
- **alice:** in the room, seen before, locked by me.
- **bob:** seen before (in the directory) but has **left**. He's hidden, and therefore locked, per #81 Criteria C.
- **carol:** in the room but **not in the directory**, so she's the first-seen collaborator (the issue's definition of "new").
- **Layering:** off, and never turned on (`null` order).
- `extra` lets a test override any field.

```ts
const ALL_DEFAULTS = ["visible", "locked", "hidden"];
```

- These are the three options from Criteria A.

### Criteria B: first-seen collaborators

**Test 1: `AC-B: with Locked, a first-seen collaborator starts visible but locked`**

```ts
const next = getNewcomerState("carol", state("locked"))!;
expect(next.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(false);
expect(next.lockedCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(true);
expect(isCollaboratorInteractive("carol", next, "me")).toBe(false);
```

- **Line 1:** carol is seen for the first time with the default set to Locked. `!` says the result isn't `null`.
- **Line 2:** "visible", so carol isn't in the hidden set.
- **Line 3:** "locked", so she is in the lock set.
- **Line 4:** under #81's rule her elements can't be interacted with.
- **Source:** Criteria B, "Locked → visible but locked".

**Test 2: `AC-B: with Visible, a first-seen collaborator starts visible and interactive`**

```ts
const next = getNewcomerState("carol", state("visible"))!;
expect(next.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(false);
expect(next.lockedCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(false);
expect(isCollaboratorInteractive("carol", next, "me")).toBe(true);
```

- Same shape as Test 1: not hidden, not locked, and interactive.
- **Source:** Criteria B, "Visible → visible and interactive".

**Test 3: `AC-B: with Hidden, a first-seen collaborator starts hidden, and therefore locked`**

```ts
const next = getNewcomerState("carol", state("hidden"))!;
expect(next.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(true);
expect(next.lockedCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(true);
expect(isCollaboratorInteractive("carol", next, "me")).toBe(false);
```

- Hidden, and also in the lock set. That's #81's rule: hiding also locks, so she stays locked if she's shown later.
- **Source:** Criteria B, "Hidden → hidden (and therefore locked, per #81)".

**Test 4: `AC-B: the default changes only the newcomer, not anyone else`**

```ts
for (const mode of ALL_DEFAULTS) {
  const next = getNewcomerState("carol", state(mode))!;
  const others = (ids) => [...ids].filter((id) => id !== "carol").sort();
  expect(others(next.hiddenCollaboratorIds)).toEqual(["bob"]);
  expect(others(next.lockedCollaboratorIds)).toEqual(["alice", "bob"]);
}
```

- For each of the three defaults, carol is applied.
- `others` drops carol and sorts what's left.
- Everyone else's state must be exactly what it was before: bob hidden; alice and bob locked.
- **Source:** Criteria B, "they start in the chosen state". Only the newcomer is mentioned.

**Test 5: `AC-B: a collaborator seen before is not affected when they rejoin, even after leaving`**

```ts
for (const mode of ALL_DEFAULTS) {
  expect(getNewcomerState("bob", state(mode))).toBe(null);
}
```

- bob is in the directory but not in the room: he left and is rejoining.
- `null` means no change, under all three defaults.
- **Source:** Criteria B, "A collaborator seen before (in the directory, even if they left) is not affected when they rejoin."

**Test 6: `AC-B: a collaborator seen before and still in the room is not affected`**

```ts
for (const mode of ALL_DEFAULTS) {
  expect(getNewcomerState("alice", state(mode))).toBe(null);
}
```

- Same as Test 5, for someone who never left. This matters because `updateCollaborator` runs on every pointer move.
- **Source:** Criteria B, plus the resolved question "Who is new?" (not in the directory yet).

**Test 7: `decision (Q4): a first-seen collaborator's leftover state is replaced by the chosen state`**

```ts
const leftover = {
  hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["bob", "carol"]),
  lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice", "bob", "carol"]),
};
const visible = getNewcomerState("carol", state("visible", leftover))!;
expect(visible.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(false);
expect(visible.lockedCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(false);
const locked = getNewcomerState("carol", state("locked", leftover))!;
expect(locked.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(false);
expect(locked.lockedCollaboratorIds.has("carol")).toBe(true);
```

# 4. `collaboratorSettings.test.ts` (new, 18 tests)

[excalidraw-app/tests/collaboratorSettings.test.ts](excalidraw-app/tests/collaboratorSettings.test.ts)

### Shared setup

```ts
import { STORAGE_KEYS } from "../app_constants";
import {
  loadCollaboratorSettings,
  saveCollaboratorSettings,
} from "../collab/collaboratorSettings";
const KEY = STORAGE_KEYS.LOCAL_STORAGE_COLLABORATOR_SETTINGS;
```

- The module and the key don't exist yet; Phase 3 adds them.
- The key is defined in the same place as #116's `LOCAL_STORAGE_COLLABORATOR_DIRECTORY`.

```ts
const DEFAULTS = {
  newCollaboratorDefault: "locked",
  hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
  lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
  collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
  collaboratorLayerOrder: null,
};
```

- **`"locked"`:** from Criteria A ("defaults to Locked").
- **The rest:** the existing defaults from #116, #81 and #82 (nobody hidden or locked, layering off, no order).

```ts
const CHANGED = {
  newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
  hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["bob"]),
  lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice", "bob"]),
  collaboratorLayeringEnabled: true,
  collaboratorLayerOrder: ["alice", "me", "bob", "__unknown__"],
};
```

- Every one of the five settings is different from its default, so a round trip proves each one is saved.

```ts
const readStored = () => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)!);
const writeStored = (value) => localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(value));
beforeEach(() => localStorage.clear());
afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks());
```

- These read and write the raw storage entry.
- Each test starts with empty storage, and the storage spies are removed after each test.

### Criteria F: remembered

**Test 1: `AC-F: every setting round-trips as I left it`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(CHANGED);
```

- Save all five settings, load them back, and they're the same. A reload is exactly that: save, then load.
- **Source:** Criteria F, "restored as I left them".

**Test 2: `AC-F: hidden and locked collaborators come back as sets`**

```ts
expect(loaded.hiddenCollaboratorIds).toBeInstanceOf(Set);
expect(loaded.lockedCollaboratorIds).toBeInstanceOf(Set);
```

- `JSON` can't store a `Set`, which is what caused the `{}` freeze in #82. The rest of the editor calls `.has()` on these, so they must be rebuilt as real Sets.
- **Source:** Criteria F, plus your rule to serialize Sets explicitly.

**Test 3: `AC-F: the newcomer default is one preference for all rooms`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings(
  "room-a",
  { ...DEFAULTS, newCollaboratorDefault: "visible" },
  "me",
);
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-b", "me")).toEqual({
  ...DEFAULTS,
  newCollaboratorDefault: "visible",
});
```

- Visible is chosen in room A, and room B (never saved) loads Visible too. Everything else in room B is the default.
- **Source:** Criteria F, "The newcomer default is one preference for all rooms."

**Test 4: `AC-F: hidden, locked, the Layering switch and the order are saved per room`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-b", { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["carol"]), lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["carol"]), collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false, collaboratorLayerOrder: null }, "me");
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(CHANGED);
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-b", "me")).toEqual({ ...CHANGED, hidden: carol, locked: carol, off, null });
```

- Two rooms get different per-room settings. Each loads its own, and saving room B doesn't overwrite room A.
- **Source:** Criteria F, "the other settings are saved per room, like #116's directory".

**Test 5: `AC-F: a room's settings don't carry into a room never saved`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-new", "me")).toEqual({
  ...DEFAULTS,
  newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
});
```

- A brand-new room gets the defaults, except for the one global preference.
- This is also the case that fixes today's leak of lock and layering state between rooms.

**Test 6: `Design: sets are stored as plain arrays in one versioned entry`**

```ts
const stored = readStored();
expect(typeof stored.version).toBe("number");
expect(JSON.stringify(stored)).toContain('["bob"]');
expect(JSON.stringify(stored)).toContain('["alice","bob"]');
```

- The entry has a version number, and the hidden and locked Sets are written as arrays, not `{}`.
- **Source:** the Design comment ("one small module with a version number"), plus your Set/Map rule.

**Test 7: `Design: collaborators who never returned are kept in the room's entry`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings(
  "room-a",
  { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["long-gone"]) },
  "me",
);
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me").hiddenCollaboratorIds).toEqual(
  new Set(["long-gone"]),
);
```

- An id that may never come back isn't pruned on save or load.
- "Ignored if unknown" is the editor's job: their elements fall into Miscellaneous. That's tested in Phase 4.
- **Source:** the Design comment's Consequences, "kept in the room's entry (small) and ignored if unknown".

**Test 8: `Design: keeps only the 20 most recently used rooms, like #116's directory`**

```ts
for (let i = 0; i < 25; i++)
  saveCollaboratorSettings(`room-${i}`, CHANGED, "me");
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-24", "me")).toEqual(CHANGED);
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-0", "me")).toEqual({
  ...DEFAULTS,
  newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
});
```

- After saving 25 rooms, the newest is kept and the oldest has been dropped. It falls back to the defaults, but the global default survives.
- **Source:** "other". This matches #116's 20-room limit, using the shared pruning helper we agreed to extract, and keeps the entry small as the Design says.

### Criteria I: safe restore

**Test 9: `(control) hiding a collaborator other than me is restored`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]) }, "me");
expect(load(...).hiddenCollaboratorIds).toEqual(new Set(["alice"]));
```

- This is the control for Tests 10 and 11. Hidden collaborators other than me are restored, so the next test can't pass just because nothing is restored.

**Test 10: `AC-I: hiding my own drawings is not restored`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", { ...CHANGED, hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["me", "alice"]) }, "me");
expect(load(...).hiddenCollaboratorIds).toEqual(new Set(["alice"]));
```

- **Setup:** "Hide all" also hides me, which forces view mode (#116).
- After a reload, alice is still hidden and I'm not, so the room doesn't open stuck in view mode.
- **Source:** Criteria I, "Hiding my own drawings is not restored on reload."

**Test 11: `AC-I: my own id saved as hidden (e.g. saved without knowing me) is dropped on load`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", { ..., hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["me", "alice"]) }, null);
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me").hiddenCollaboratorIds).toEqual(new Set(["alice"]));
```

- The save didn't know my id (`null`), so `me` was stored. Load knows it's me and drops it.
- This is the second safety net: even if bad data was saved, the room never opens stuck in view mode.
- **Source:** Criteria I.

**Test 12: `AC-I: nothing saved → the defaults (newcomers Locked)`**

```ts
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
```

- Empty storage gives the defaults, which is the first-ever visit.
- **Source:** Criteria I ("falling back to the defaults") and Criteria A (Locked).

**Test 13: `AC-I: unreadable data → the defaults, without throwing`**

```ts
localStorage.setItem(KEY, "not json");          → DEFAULTS
writeStored(["not", "settings"]);               → DEFAULTS
writeStored(null);                              → DEFAULTS
```

- Three kinds of junk: invalid JSON, an array instead of an object, and `null`.
- Each one returns the defaults instead of throwing. A throw here would break joining the room.
- **Source:** Criteria I, "unreadable … ignored without errors, falling back to the defaults".

**Test 14: `AC-I: data from an older version → the defaults`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
const stored = readStored();
writeStored({ ...stored, version: stored.version - 1 });   → DEFAULTS
const { version: _version, ...withoutVersion } = stored;
writeStored(withoutVersion);                               → DEFAULTS
```

- The test takes a valid entry, then (a) lowers its version by one and (b) removes the version entirely.
- Both are treated as older data, so the defaults come back even though the rest of the data is valid.
- **Source:** Criteria I, "or from an older version".

**Test 15: `AC-I: settings with the wrong shape fall back to their defaults`**

```ts
writeStored({
  ...stored,
  newcomerDefault: "purple",
  rooms: {
    "room-a": {
      updated: 1,
      hidden: "bob",
      locked: [1, 2],
      layeringEnabled: "yes",
      layerOrder: { 0: "alice" },
    },
  },
});
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
```

- The version is valid, but every field has the wrong type:
  - the newcomer default isn't one of the three options;
  - hidden is a string, not an array;
  - locked is an array of numbers, not ids;
  - the switch is a string, not a boolean;
  - the order is an object, not an array.
- Each field falls back to its own default.
- This test fixes the stored field names in place, as I noted at the checkpoint.

**Test 16: `AC-I: a broken room list keeps the newcomer default`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me");
writeStored({ ...readStored(), rooms: "broken" });
expect(load(...)).toEqual({ ...DEFAULTS, newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" });
```

- Corrupt per-room data doesn't take the valid global preference down with it.
- **Source:** Criteria I (fall back without errors), applied to each setting separately.

**Test 17: `AC-I: saving doesn't throw when storage is unavailable`**

```ts
const setItem = vi.spyOn(localStorage, "setItem").mockImplementation(() => {
  throw new Error("quota exceeded");
});
expect(() => saveCollaboratorSettings("room-a", CHANGED, "me")).not.toThrow();
expect(setItem).toHaveBeenCalled();
```

- This simulates a full or blocked storage.
- The save must not throw, because it runs from the app's `onChange` on every change.
- The last line proves it actually tried to save, so the test isn't passing because nothing happened.
- The spy pattern is copied from #116's directory test.

**Test 18: `AC-I: loading doesn't throw when storage is unavailable`**

```ts
vi.spyOn(localStorage, "getItem").mockImplementation(() => {
  throw new Error("blocked");
});
expect(loadCollaboratorSettings("room-a", "me")).toEqual(DEFAULTS);
```

- With reads blocked (e.g. a private window), loading gives the defaults and doesn't throw.

```text
};

/** structurally satisfied by the editor's AppState */
export type CreatorVisibility = {
  /**
   * creator ids hidden on this client. `UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID` hides the
   * miscellaneous bucket.
   */
  hiddenCollaboratorIds?: ReadonlySet<string>;
  /**
   * creators this client can name (seen at some point). Stamped creators
   * missing from it are treated as unknown (miscellaneous). `null`/omitted
   * (e.g. outside of a room) → every stamped creator is its own bucket.
   */
  collaboratorDirectory?: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown> | null;
```

```typescript
/**
 * The collaborator dropdown's saved settings (#83), next to #116's
 * per-room collaborator directory: one global preference (how newcomers
 * start) and, per room, hidden and locked collaborators, the Layering switch
 * and the layer order.
 *
 * Stored locally only, in one versioned entry. The matching AppState fields
 * are never persisted with the scene, exported or synced; this module is the
 * only place they're saved. Hiding my own drawings is never saved or
 * restored, so a room never opens stuck in view mode.
 */

import { DEFAULT_NEW_COLLABORATOR } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { NewCollaboratorDefault } from "@excalidraw/element";
import type { AppState } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/types";

import { STORAGE_KEYS } from "../app_constants";

import { readStoredObject, withRecentRooms } from "./collaboratorDirectory";

/** bump when the stored shape changes; other versions are ignored */
const VERSION = 1;

const NEW_COLLABORATOR_DEFAULTS: readonly unknown[] = [
  "visible",
  "locked",
  "hidden",
] satisfies NewCollaboratorDefault[];

export type CollaboratorSettings = Pick<
  AppState,
  | "newCollaboratorDefault"
  | "hiddenCollaboratorIds"
  | "lockedCollaboratorIds"
  | "collaboratorLayeringEnabled"
  | "collaboratorLayerOrder"
>;

type StoredRoom = {
  updated: number;
  hidden: string[];
  locked: string[];
  layeringEnabled: boolean;
  layerOrder: readonly string[] | null;
};

const isIdList = (value: unknown): value is string[] =>
  Array.isArray(value) && value.every((id) => typeof id === "string");

const readSettings = () => {
  const stored = readStoredObject(
    STORAGE_KEYS.LOCAL_STORAGE_COLLABORATOR_SETTINGS,
  );
  return stored.version === VERSION ? stored : {};
};

/**
 * The saved settings for `roomId`. Anything missing, unreadable or from
 * another version falls back to its default; `selfId` is never restored as
 * hidden.
 */
export const loadCollaboratorSettings = (
  roomId: string,
  selfId: string | null,
): CollaboratorSettings => {
  const stored = readSettings();
  const room = stored.rooms?.[roomId];
  return {
    newCollaboratorDefault: NEW_COLLABORATOR_DEFAULTS.includes(
      stored.newcomerDefault,
    )
      ? stored.newcomerDefault
      : DEFAULT_NEW_COLLABORATOR,
    hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(
      isIdList(room?.hidden) ? room.hidden.filter((id) => id !== selfId) : [],
    ),
    lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(isIdList(room?.locked) ? room.locked : []),
    collaboratorLayeringEnabled: room?.layeringEnabled === true,
    collaboratorLayerOrder: isIdList(room?.layerOrder) ? room.layerOrder : null,
  };
};

/** saves the settings (the newcomer default for all rooms, the rest for `roomId`) */
export const saveCollaboratorSettings = (
  roomId: string,
  settings: CollaboratorSettings,
  selfId: string | null,
) => {
  const currentRoom: StoredRoom = {
    updated: Date.now(),
    hidden: [...settings.hiddenCollaboratorIds].filter((id) => id !== selfId),
    locked: [...settings.lockedCollaboratorIds],
    layeringEnabled: settings.collaboratorLayeringEnabled,
    layerOrder: settings.collaboratorLayerOrder,
  };
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(
      STORAGE_KEYS.LOCAL_STORAGE_COLLABORATOR_SETTINGS,
      JSON.stringify({
        version: VERSION,
        newcomerDefault: settings.newCollaboratorDefault,
        rooms: withRecentRooms(readSettings().rooms, roomId, currentRoom),
      }),
    );
  } catch {
    // storage unavailable — settings stay in memory for this session
  }
};

```

```text
tsc exit: 0
+/**
+ * Returns `order` with `ids` added directly above the miscellaneous bucket,
+ * in the given (join) order (#83 D). My own id goes on top instead, like in
+ * the default order. Ids already in `order` are moved, never duplicated.
+ */
+const addToLayerOrder = (
+  order: readonly string[],
+  ids: readonly string[],
+  selfId: string | null,
+): string[] => {
+  const next = order.filter((id) => !ids.includes(id));
+  const miscIndex = next.indexOf(UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID);
+  next.splice(
+    miscIndex === -1 ? next.length : miscIndex,
+    0,
+    ...ids.filter((id) => id !== selfId),
+  );
+  return selfId !== null && ids.includes(selfId) ? [selfId, ...next] : next;
+};
+
```

## Summary

- **Pure logic** in [ownership.ts](packages/element/src/ownership.ts):
  - **`getNewcomerState(id, state)`:** returns `null` for anyone already in the directory, for me, and for Miscellaneous. Otherwise it applies the chosen default; the locking reuses #81's `addLockedCollaborators`, so hiding also locks. It replaces leftover state (Q4) and places the newcomer in a stored layer order, if one exists.
  - **`getCollaboratorLayerOrder` (#82):** newcomers now go directly above Miscellaneous, in join order; my own id goes on top (Q2). Both functions share one private helper, `addToLayerOrder`.
  - **`NEW_COLLABORATOR_DEFAULTS` and `DEFAULT_NEW_COLLABORATOR = "locked"`:** the list of options and the default, defined once. The type, the AppState default, the storage validation and Phase 5's radio buttons all use them.
- **AppState:** a new `newCollaboratorDefault` field, default `"locked"`. Its `browser`, `export` and `server` flags are all `false`.
- **Persistence:** new [collaboratorSettings.ts](excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorSettings.ts), with `loadCollaboratorSettings` and `saveCollaboratorSettings`.
  - One entry, `excalidraw-collaborator-settings`: `{version: 1, newcomerDefault, rooms}`. The global default is separate from the per-room settings.

  - My own id is removed from the hidden list on both save and load.
- **Shared room helpers:** #116's room pruning moved out of [collaboratorDirectory.ts](excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorDirectory.ts) into `readStoredObject` and `withRecentRooms`, used by both modules. #116's behavior is unchanged and its 12 directory tests pass.

```text
}));

vi.mock("socket.io-client", () => ({

      mocks.handlers.set(event, handler);
    },
    once: () => {},
    off: () => {},
    emit: (...args: any[]) => {
      mocks.emitted.push(args);
    },
    close: () => {},
  }),
}));

// all exports mocked explicitly: spreading `importOriginal()` here deadlocks
// the app's module initialization
vi.mock("@excalidraw/excalidraw/data/encryption", () => ({

  generateEncryptionKey: async () => "test-room-key",
  encryptData: async (_key: string, data: Uint8Array) => ({
    encryptedBuffer: data,

  decryptData: async (_iv: Uint8Array, data: ArrayBuffer) => data,
}));

vi.mock("../data/firebase", () => ({

const getCreatorId = (id: string) =>

/** messages this client broadcast (decoded) */
const getSentMessages = () =>
  mocks.emitted
    .filter(([event]) => event === WS_EVENTS.SERVER)
    .map(([, , buffer]) => JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(buffer)));

const getSentOfType = (type: WS_SUBTYPES) =>
  getSentMessages().filter((message) => message.type === type);

// NOTE: server events are awaited directly (not inside an async `act`), which
// would also wait for the room's 5s initialization fallback timer. Callers
// assert through `waitFor`.

/** simulates a message from another client arriving through the room */
const deliver = async (
  message: SocketUpdateDataSource[keyof SocketUpdateDataSource],
) => {
  await mocks.handlers.get("client-broadcast")!(
    new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(message)),
    new Uint8Array(12),
  );
};

const triggerServerEvent = async (event: string, ...args: any[]) => {
  await mocks.handlers.get(event)!(...args);
};

/** local changes reach Collab through onChange → syncElements */
const sync = () => {
  act(() => {
    window.collab.syncElements(h.app.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted());
  });
};

/**
 * Returns the scene promise wrapped in an object: returning it directly from
 * this async function would make callers wait for the room's scene, which
 * only arrives after the "first-in-room" event they still have to send.
 */
const startCollaboration = async (
  roomLinkData: { roomId: string; roomKey: string } | null = null,
) => {
  let scenePromise!: ReturnType<typeof window.collab.startCollaboration>;
  act(() => {
    scenePromise = window.collab.startCollaboration(roomLinkData);
  });
  await waitFor(() => expect(mocks.handlers.has("first-in-room")).toBe(true));
  return { scenePromise };
};

/** start a new room and finish initialization (we're alone in it) */
const startNewRoom = async () => {
  await startCollaboration();

  await waitFor(() =>
    expect(window.collab.portal.socketInitialized).toBe(true),
  );
};

const getClientId = () => window.collab.getClientId()!;
```
