```typescript
  await render(<ExcalidrawApp />);
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

describe("newcomer default — Criteria A and B (first-seen collaborators)", () => {
  it("AC-A: in a room, the New collaborators setting starts as Locked", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("locked");
  });

  it("AC-B: by default, a collaborator joining for the first time starts visible but locked", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    await peerJoins("alice");
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("AC-B: with Visible, a collaborator joining for the first time starts visible and interactive", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "visible" });
    await peerJoins("alice");
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
  });

  it("AC-B: with Hidden, a collaborator joining for the first time starts hidden (and therefore locked)", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" });
    await peerJoins("alice");
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(true);
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("AC-B: a collaborator first seen through a pointer message starts in the default too", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    await deliver({
      type: WS_SUBTYPES.MOUSE_LOCATION,
      payload: {
        socketId: "bob-socket" as SocketId,
        pointer: { x: 0, y: 0, tool: "pointer" },
        button: "up",
        selectedElementIds: {},
        username: "Bob",
        clientId: "bob",
      },
    });
    await waitFor(() => expect(isLocked("bob")).toBe(true));
  });

  it("AC-B: a collaborator who leaves and rejoins keeps the settings I gave them", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    await peerJoins("alice");
    execute("toggleCollaboratorLock", "alice");
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);

    await roomMembersAre();
    await peerJoins("alice", "alice-socket-2");

    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
  });

  it("AC-B: a collaborator seen in an earlier session isn't new (control: one never seen is)", async () => {
    saveCollaboratorDirectory(
      ROOM.roomId,
      new Map([["alice", { username: "alice", lastSeen: Date.now() }]]),
    );
    await joinRoom(ROOM);

    await peerJoins("alice");
    await peerJoins("bob");

    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
    // (control) bob was never seen in this room
    expect(isLocked("bob")).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("newcomer default — Criteria C (only future newcomers)", () => {
  it("AC-C: changing the setting doesn't change collaborators already seen", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    await peerJoins("alice");

    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" });
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);

    // (control) the new setting does apply to the next newcomer
    await peerJoins("bob");
    expect(isHidden("bob")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("AC-C: Show all and Unlock all still work for collaborators already seen", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" });
    await peerJoins("alice");
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(true);

    execute("showAllCollaborators");
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
    // #81 C: shown again → still locked until unlocked
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);

    execute("unlockAllCollaborators");
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("newcomer default — Criteria D (layer order)", () => {
  it("AC-D: with layering on, newcomers land directly above miscellaneous, in join order", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    execute("toggleCollaboratorLayering");

    await peerJoins("alice");
    await peerJoins("bob");

    expect(h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder).toEqual([
      getClientId(),
      "alice",
      "bob",
      UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
    ]);
  });
});

describe("newcomer default — Criteria E (me)", () => {
  it("AC-E: with Hidden saved as the default, my own drawings are never hidden (control: a newcomer is)", async () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      "any-room",
      {
        newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
        hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
        lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: null,
      },
      null,
    );
    await startNewRoom();
    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("hidden");

    expect(isHidden(getClientId())).toBe(false);
    expect(isLocked(getClientId())).toBe(false);
    expect(h.state.viewModeEnabled).toBe(false);

    // (control)
    await peerJoins("alice");
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("saved settings — Criteria F (remembered across reloads)", () => {
  it("AC-F: after a reload, hidden, locked, the Layering switch, the order and the newcomer default are restored", async () => {
    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    await peerJoins("alice");
    await peerJoins("bob");
    execute("toggleCollaboratorVisibility", "bob");
    execute("toggleCollaboratorLayering");
    execute("moveCollaboratorLayer", { id: "bob", toIndex: 0 });
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "visible" });
    const me = getClientId();
    const order = [...h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder!];
    expect(order[0]).toBe("bob");

    await openRoomLink(ROOM);

    expect(getClientId()).toBe(me);
    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("visible");
    expect([...h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds]).toEqual(["bob"]);
    expect([...h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds].sort()).toEqual(["alice", "bob"]);
    expect(h.state.collaboratorLayeringEnabled).toBe(true);
    expect(h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder).toEqual(order);
  });

  it("AC-F: a rejoining collaborator keeps their settings after a reload", async () => {
    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    await peerJoins("alice");
    execute("toggleCollaboratorLock", "alice");

    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    await peerJoins("alice");

    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
  });

  it("AC-F: settings are per room: another room opens with its own settings, the newcomer default with me", async () => {
    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    await peerJoins("alice");
    execute("toggleCollaboratorVisibility", "alice");
    execute("toggleCollaboratorLayering");
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" });

    await openRoomLink(OTHER_ROOM);

    expect(h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds.size).toBe(0);
    expect(h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds.size).toBe(0);
    expect(h.state.collaboratorLayeringEnabled).toBe(false);
    expect(h.state.collaboratorLayerOrder).toBe(null);
    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("hidden");
  });
});

describe("saved settings — Criteria I (safe restore)", () => {
  it("(control) hiding my own drawings puts me in view mode", async () => {
    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    await peerJoins("alice");
    execute("hideAllCollaborators");
    expect(isHidden(getClientId())).toBe(true);
    expect(h.state.viewModeEnabled).toBe(true);
  });

  it("AC-I: after a reload, hiding my own drawings is not restored, so the room doesn't open in view mode", async () => {
    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    await peerJoins("alice");
    execute("hideAllCollaborators");

    await openRoomLink(ROOM);

    expect(isHidden(getClientId())).toBe(false);
    expect(h.state.viewModeEnabled).toBe(false);
    // the rest of Hide all is restored
    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("AC-I: unreadable saved settings are ignored: the room opens with the defaults", async () => {
    localStorage.setItem(
      STORAGE_KEYS.LOCAL_STORAGE_COLLABORATOR_SETTINGS,
      "{not json",
    );
    await joinRoom(ROOM);

    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("locked");
    expect(h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds.size).toBe(0);
    expect(h.state.collaboratorLayeringEnabled).toBe(false);
    await peerJoins("alice");
    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);
  });

  it("AC-I: saved settings for a collaborator no longer known are ignored", async () => {
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      ROOM.roomId,
      {
        newCollaboratorDefault: "locked",
        hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["ghost"]),
        lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["ghost"]),
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: true,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: ["ghost", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID],
      },
      null,
    );
    await joinRoom(ROOM);
    await receivePeerElement("ghost-rect", "ghost");

    // ghost isn't in this client's directory: their drawing counts as
    // miscellaneous (#116), which isn't hidden
    expect(
      excludeElementsByHiddenCreators(h.elements, h.state).map((el) => el.id),
    ).toContain("ghost-rect");
  });
});

describe("newcomer default and saved settings — Criteria G and H (local only, shared state untouched)", () => {
  it("(control) a local edit is sent to the room and changes the shared state", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    await receivePeerElement("theirs", "alice");
    const sentBefore = getSentUpdates().length;
    const sharedBefore = getShared();

    API.updateScene({
      elements: syncInvalidIndices([
        ...h.app.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted(),
        API.createElement({ id: "mine" }),
      ]),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY,
    });
    sync();

    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(getSentUpdates().length).toBeGreaterThan(sentBefore),
    );
    expect(getShared()).not.toEqual(sharedBefore);
  });

  it("AC-H: applying the default and changing the setting send nothing and change no element", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    await receivePeerElement("theirs", "alice");
    const sentBefore = getSentUpdates().length;
    const sharedBefore = getShared();

    await peerJoins("alice");
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" });
    await peerJoins("bob");
    sync();

    expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);
    expect(isHidden("bob")).toBe(true);
    expect(getSentUpdates().length).toBe(sentBefore);
    expect(getShared()).toEqual(sharedBefore);
  });

  it("AC-H: restoring saved settings on join sends nothing and changes no element", async () => {
    mocks.storedRoomElements = syncInvalidIndices([
      stamp(API.createElement({ id: "theirs" }), "alice"),
    ]);
    saveCollaboratorSettings(
      ROOM.roomId,
      {
        newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden",
        hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]),
        lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]),
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: true,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: ["alice", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID],
      },
      null,
    );

    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    sync();

    expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(true);
    expect(getSentUpdates()).toEqual([]);
    const stored = mocks.storedRoomElements[0];
    expect(getShared()).toEqual([
      {
        id: "theirs",
        index: stored.index,
        version: stored.version,
        versionNonce: stored.versionNonce,
      },
    ]);
  });

  it("AC-G: applying the default and restoring add no undo history entries", async () => {
    await openRoomLink(ROOM);
    const undoBefore = API.getUndoStack().length;

    await peerJoins("alice");
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "visible" });
    await peerJoins("bob");

    expect(API.getUndoStack().length).toBe(undoBefore);
  });

  it("AC-G: the newcomer default is never saved with the scene, exported or sent to the server", async () => {
    await startNewRoom();
    API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "hidden" });

    expect(clearAppStateForLocalStorage(h.state)).not.toHaveProperty(
      "newCollaboratorDefault",
    );
    expect(cleanAppStateForExport(h.state)).not.toHaveProperty(
      "newCollaboratorDefault",
    );
    expect(clearAppStateForDatabase(h.state)).not.toHaveProperty(
      "newCollaboratorDefault",
    );
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 21:04:47Z)**_

Phase 4 is done: newcomers now get the default when they first appear, and each room's settings are saved and come back after a reload. The tests pass, and they fail when the wiring is removed. There are two commits: `f0823ed6` (your revised Q1) and `71ddae90` (the wiring).

## What changed

**Q1 revision (`f0823ed6`):** newcomers go directly above Miscellaneous only while Miscellaneous is the bottom row. If you've moved it up, they go to the very bottom. The two tests for that case were updated to match.

**The wiring (`71ddae90`):**

- **Applying the default:** in `Collab.updateCollaborator`, someone not yet in the directory gets `getNewcomerState`.
  - The result is merged into the `updateScene` call that was already there, so there's no extra update.
  - `recordSighting` is unchanged.
  - The cheap `directory.has` check runs first, so a normal pointer move never reads the full AppState.
- **Restoring:**
  - In `startCollaboration`, the room's saved settings replace the old `hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set()` inside the existing `updateScene`.
  - Both `resetScene()` calls on join now go through `resetSceneKeepingSettings`, which resets, puts the saved settings back right away, and blocks saving in between. This closes the race from Phase 1.
- **Saving:** the app's existing `onChange` calls `collabAPI.saveCollaboratorSettings(appState)`, next to `syncElements`.
  - It only compares the five settings by reference, so it writes only when a setting actually changed.
  - As a side effect, lock and layering settings no longer carry over into the next room.
- **Q3:** retitled #81's "AC-G: lock settings reset when the page reloads" and #82's "AC-F: the layer order resets when the page reloads". They now say "…not restored from the scene's local save (#83 F)". I also renamed their `describe` blocks from "(local and non-persistent)" to "(local only; saved by the host app per #83)", and updated #82's header comment. The test bodies are unchanged.

## New tests: `collabNewcomer.test.tsx` (24 tests)

These run through the real app, Collab and Portal. **Reloads are real:** the test unmounts the app and renders it again on the room link, keeping local and session storage, so the app joins the room through the normal page-load path.

- **A:** in a room, the setting starts as Locked.
- **B:**
  - Locked, Visible and Hidden each work as specified.
  - Someone first seen through a pointer message (not just the identity message) gets the default too.
  - A collaborator who leaves and rejoins keeps the settings I gave them.
  - Someone seen in an earlier session isn't new, with a control showing a never-seen collaborator is.
  - With Visible, a newcomer's leftover saved lock is cleared (Q4).
- **C:**
  - Changing the setting doesn't touch anyone already seen, with a control showing the next newcomer does get it.
  - Show all and Unlock all still work.
- **D:** with layering on, alice and then bob land in the order `[me, alice, bob, Miscellaneous]`.
- **E:** with Hidden saved as the default, I'm never hidden and not put in view mode, with a control showing a newcomer is hidden.
- **F:**
  - After a reload, hidden, locked, the Layering switch, the order and the default all come back, and my client id is unchanged.
  - A rejoining collaborator keeps their lock after a reload.
  - Settings are per room: another room opens with its own settings, and only the newcomer default carries over.
- **I:**
  - Hiding my own drawings isn't restored, so the room doesn't open in view mode, with a control showing hiding myself does turn on view mode.
  - Unreadable saved data opens the room with the defaults.
  - A saved collaborator nobody knows any more is ignored, while the rest of that room's settings are still restored.
- **G / H:**
  - With a control showing a local edit is sent and does change elements:
    - applying the default and changing the setting send nothing and change no element;
    - restoring on join sends nothing and leaves `index`, `version` and `versionNonce` as stored.
  - No undo entries are added.
  - The newcomer default never appears in the scene's local save, in exports, or in what's sent to the server.

**Checking the tests depend on the wiring:** with `Collab.tsx` and `App.tsx` stashed, 19 of 24 fail. The 5 that still pass are the two controls, the AppState default (A), the AppState flags (G), and "with Visible". "Visible" looks the same as "nothing happened", so the leftover-lock test above is what proves it.

## Test-writing problems I caught and fixed

- **Two tests passed for the wrong reason:** "Hide all" only hides collaborators who have drawings, so in my first version I was never hidden. The control test failed and exposed it. Both tests now hide my own row directly.
- **The editor didn't know which collaborator was me:** the room setup now simulates the server's member list on join, as the real server does.
- **Four tests were too weak:** they passed even with the wiring removed. They now also assert that the feature actually ran.
- **A timing wait was too short:** the wait for the room to start on a reload now has a 5-second limit instead of 1 second, with a comment explaining why. Before that change, 1 of 8 runs failed.

## Test results

- **Collaborator suites:** `Test Files 25 passed (25) · Tests 574 passed (574)`. `tsc` exits 0, ESLint is clean, and Prettier ran on the changed files.
- **Full suite:** `Tests 4 failed | 2709 passed | 47 skipped`.
  - 3 are the known Windows `exportToSvg` snapshots.
  - The 4th is `zindex › send back`, which has now failed in 2 of 4 full runs. It passes 20/20 on its own.
  - It's the first test in its file timing out while the app loads. The pre-#83 code has the same problem: running `packages/element/tests` alone gives 16 failures on the old code and about 15 on mine, all first-test-in-file timeouts.
  - So it's this machine under load, not this change. CI should confirm.

## Not sure about

1. **Q2:** I kept "my own new id goes on top". If "stick with what was before" meant #82's original behavior (newcomers at the bottom, me included), tell me.
2. **When the newcomer default is applied for older clients:** clients without #116's ids are only seen when they send a pointer, identity or idle message, so the default applies then, not at the moment they join.
3. **My other tabs:** a second tab of mine has a different client id, so it's treated as a newcomer and locked by default. That matches Criteria B as written.

**Tech debt**

- _Introduced:_
  - The settings module and the directory share the room-pruning helpers.
  - An older stored version is dropped on the next save; there's no migration.
  - `collabNewcomer.test.tsx` copies about 60 lines of socket, encryption and Firebase mocks; `vi.mock` only works per file, as in #81 and #82.
  - The typed `appState` variable in `updateCollaborator` works around `updateScene`'s key inference.
- _Encountered:_
  - `resetScene` wipes collaborator state on join; now handled.
  - Lock and layering leaking between rooms; now fixed.
  - The directory reloads newest-first.
  - #116's room pruning keeps the older room when two saves share a millisecond.
  - The first test in a file times out under load (`zindex`, element tests).
  - The repo's Prettier version can't parse `satisfies`.

**DECISIONS LOG**

1. Plan: I proposed a newcomer check in `recordSighting` and separate helpers. You asked for no bloat and reuse of #81–84, so the check went in `updateCollaborator` and the logic is built from existing helpers.
2. Q1: I proposed placing newcomers literally directly above Miscellaneous, even when it's been moved up. You first agreed, then revised it: if Miscellaneous was moved up, newcomers go to the bottom (`f0823ed6`).
3. Q2: should my own new id be treated as a newcomer or go on top? You chose on top, then said "stick with what was before", which I've kept as on top.
4. Q3: I asked whether to leave or retitle the "resets on reload" tests. You said they're wrong because these settings persist and reset only on Reset, so they're retitled.
5. Q4: should a pruned collaborator who returns get the newcomer default? Yes; it replaces leftover saved state.
6. Shared room pruning: I recommended extracting it rather than copying it. You approved extracting.
7. Test 14: I offered a `version: 0` check. You wanted it as a fallback next to "version − 1".
8. Tests 8 and 19 (no-mutation checks): I offered to rename them. You kept them as backup coverage.
9. Checkpoints: I asked whether "approved going forward" meant I could run through the remaining phases. You said stop at every phase.

**Files changed:** `excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx`, `excalidraw-app/App.tsx`, `excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorSettings.ts`, `excalidraw-app/tests/collabNewcomer.test.tsx` (new), `packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorLock.test.tsx`, `packages/excalidraw/tests/collaboratorLayer.test.tsx`. The Q1 revision changed `ownership.ts`, `ownershipNewcomer.test.ts` and `ownershipLayer.test.ts`.

```text
import {
  CaptureUpdateAction,
  addLockedCollaborators,
  getCollaboratorLayerOrder,
  getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder,
  moveCollaboratorLayer,
  toggleLockedCollaborator,
  unlockVisibleCollaborators,
} from "@excalidraw/element";

import {
  BringForwardIcon,
  BringToFrontIcon,
  eyeClosedIcon,
  eyeIcon,
  LockedIcon,
  resetIcon,
  UnlockedIcon,
} from "../components/icons";
import {
  getSelfCollaboratorId,
  getVisibilityBuckets,
} from "../scene/visibility";

import { register } from "./register";

/*
 * Local-only visibility of collaborators' drawings. These only change
 * `appState.hiddenCollaboratorIds` (never synced, never in history); hiding
 * your own drawings locks view mode (enforced in App.componentDidUpdate).
 *
 * Hiding a collaborator also locks them (#81), so they stay non-interactive
 * once shown again, until unlocked.
 */

/** toggles one visibility bucket (a creator id, or UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID) */
 * local appState (never synced, never in history, elements untouched). The
 * rules live in `element/ownership.ts`.
 */

/**
 * turns layering on or off. The first time it's turned on, the default
 * order is stored; turning it off keeps the order for when it's back on
 */
export const actionToggleCollaboratorLayering = register({
  name: "toggleCollaboratorLayering",
  label: "collaboratorLayer.toggle",
  icon: BringToFrontIcon,
  viewMode: true,
  trackEvent: { category: "collab" },
  perform(elements, appState) {
    return {
      appState: {
        ...appState,
        collaboratorLayeringEnabled: !appState.collaboratorLayeringEnabled,
        collaboratorLayerOrder:
          appState.collaboratorLayerOrder ??
          getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder(appState),
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    };
  },
});

/**
 * moves a bucket to a position in the layer order (top = 0). Used by the
 * ↑ / ↓ arrows (one place) and by dragging (any place); only while on
 */
export const actionMoveCollaboratorLayer = register<{
  id: string;
  toIndex: number;
}>({
  name: "moveCollaboratorLayer",
  label: "collaboratorLayer.move",
  icon: BringForwardIcon,
  viewMode: true,
  trackEvent: { category: "collab" },
  perform(elements, appState, value) {
    if (!value || !appState.collaboratorLayeringEnabled) {
      return false;
    }
    return {
      appState: {
        ...appState,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: moveCollaboratorLayer(
          getCollaboratorLayerOrder(appState),
          value.id,
          value.toIndex,
        ),
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    };
  },
});

/** returns the layer order to the default (me on top, then join order) */
export const actionResetCollaboratorLayerOrder = register({
  name: "resetCollaboratorLayerOrder",
  label: "collaboratorLayer.reset",
  icon: resetIcon,
  viewMode: true,
  trackEvent: { category: "collab" },
  perform(elements, appState) {
    if (!appState.collaboratorLayeringEnabled) {
      return false;
    }
    return {
      appState: {
        ...appState,
        collaboratorLayerOrder: getDefaultCollaboratorLayerOrder(appState),
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    };
  },
});

/** unlocks every visible bucket; hidden ones stay locked */
```

```text
  const dragRow = (id: string, targetId: string) => {
    const dataTransfer = {
      setData: () => {},
      setDragImage: () => {},
    };
    const handle = queryControl("handle", id)!;
    const target = getRowElement(targetId);
    fireEvent.dragStart(handle, { dataTransfer });
    fireEvent.dragEnter(target, { dataTransfer });
    fireEvent.dragOver(target, { dataTransfer });
    fireEvent.drop(target, { dataTransfer });
```

```typescript
/**
 * Issue #83 — the "New collaborators" setting in the collaborator dropdown
 * (desktop and phone). Expected values come from the acceptance criteria in
 * #83, not from running the implementation:
 *
 * - A: the dropdown has a "New collaborators" setting with three options,
 *   Visible, Locked, Hidden; it defaults to Locked
 * - C: changing it doesn't change any collaborator already seen
 * - G: local only, never in undo/redo history
 *
 * Applying the setting to newcomers and saving it across reloads is the host
 * app's job (excalidraw-app/tests/collabNewcomer.test.tsx).
 */
import React from "react";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import {
  act,
  fireEvent,
  mockBoundingClientRect,
  render,
  restoreOriginalGetBoundingClientRect,
  waitFor,
} from "./test-utils";

import type { AppState } from "../types";

const { h } = window;

// Session: me, alice (locked by me) and bob (visible), all seen before
const collaborators = new Map([
  ["my-socket", { id: "me", username: "Me", isCurrentUser: true }],
  ["alice-socket", { id: "alice", username: "Alice" }],
  ["bob-socket", { id: "bob", username: "Bob" }],
]) as unknown as AppState["collaborators"];

const collaboratorDirectory = new Map([
  ["me", { username: "Me", lastSeen: 1 }],
  ["alice", { username: "Alice", lastSeen: 1 }],
  ["bob", { username: "Bob", lastSeen: 1 }],
]);

/** the options in the order the AC lists them */
const OPTIONS = ["visible", "locked", "hidden"] as const;

const openMenu = (scope: ParentNode = document) => {
  fireEvent.click(
    scope.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
      "[data-testid='collaborator-visibility-trigger']",
    )!,
  );
};

const getRadios = () => [
  ...document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>(
    "input[name='collaborator-newcomer-default']",
  ),
];

const getRadio = (option: typeof OPTIONS[number]) =>
  getRadios()[OPTIONS.indexOf(option)];

const checkedOption = () => {
  const index = getRadios().findIndex((radio) => radio.checked);
  return index === -1 ? null : OPTIONS[index];
};

beforeEach(async () => {
  await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  act(() => {
    h.app.updateScene({ collaborators });
    API.setAppState({
      collaboratorDirectory,
      lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]),
    });
  });
});

describe("New collaborators setting — dropdown UI (desktop)", () => {
  it("AC-A: the dropdown has a New collaborators setting with Visible, Locked and Hidden", () => {
    openMenu();

    expect(
      document.querySelector(".CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__newcomers")
        ?.textContent,
    ).toContain("New collaborators");
    expect(getRadios()).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(
      getRadios().map((radio) => radio.parentElement!.textContent),
    ).toEqual(["Visible", "Locked", "Hidden"]);
  });

  it("AC-A: Locked is selected by default", () => {
    openMenu();
    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("locked");
    expect(checkedOption()).toBe("locked");
  });

  for (const option of OPTIONS) {
    it(`AC-A: choosing ${option} selects it`, () => {
      openMenu();
      // start from another option, so choosing this one is a change
      act(() => {
        API.setAppState({
          newCollaboratorDefault: option === "locked" ? "hidden" : "locked",
        });
      });
      expect(checkedOption()).not.toBe(option);

      fireEvent.click(getRadio(option));

      expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe(option);
      expect(checkedOption()).toBe(option);
    });
  }

  it("AC-C: choosing an option doesn't change collaborators already seen", () => {
    openMenu();
    const lockedBefore = h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds;
    const hiddenBefore = h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds;

    for (const option of ["hidden", "visible", "locked"] as const) {
      fireEvent.click(getRadio(option));
      expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe(option);
      expect([...h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds]).toEqual(["alice"]);
      expect(h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds.size).toBe(0);
    }
    // not even copied: the same sets as before
    expect(h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds).toBe(lockedBefore);
    expect(h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds).toBe(hiddenBefore);
  });

  it("AC-G: choosing an option adds no undo history entries", () => {
    openMenu();
    const undoBefore = API.getUndoStack().length;

    fireEvent.click(getRadio("hidden"));
    fireEvent.click(getRadio("visible"));

    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("visible");
    expect(API.getUndoStack().length).toBe(undoBefore);
  });
});

describe("New collaborators setting — dropdown UI (phone)", () => {
  beforeAll(() => {
    mockBoundingClientRect({ height: 400, width: 800 });
  });

  afterAll(() => {
    restoreOriginalGetBoundingClientRect();
  });

  it("AC-A: the setting is in the main menu's collaborator section, and choosing an option selects it", async () => {
    act(() => {
      h.app.refreshEditorInterface();
    });
    expect(h.app.editorInterface.formFactor).toBe("phone");

    fireEvent.click(document.querySelector(".main-menu-trigger")!);
    const row = await waitFor(() => {
      const element = document.querySelector(".UserList-Wrapper__row");
      expect(element).not.toBe(null);
      return element!;
    });
    openMenu(row);

    expect(checkedOption()).toBe("locked");
    fireEvent.click(getRadio("hidden"));
    expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("hidden");
    expect(checkedOption()).toBe("hidden");
  });
});
```

```cjs
// #83 real-browser check: two Edge profiles (separate localStorage) in one room
const path = require("path");
const crypto = require("crypto");
const fs = require("fs");
const os = require("os");
const puppeteer = require("C:/Users/super/excalidraw/node_modules/puppeteer-core");

const EDGE = "C:/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe";
const OUT = __dirname;
const roomId = crypto.randomBytes(10).toString("hex");
const roomKey = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString("base64url");
const URL = `http://localhost:3001/#room=${roomId},${roomKey}`;

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
const log = (...args) => console.log(...args);

const launch = (name) =>
  puppeteer.launch({
    executablePath: EDGE,
    headless: "new",
    userDataDir: fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), `edge-83-${name}-`)),
    defaultViewport: { width: 1280, height: 800 },
  });

const state = (page) =>
  page.evaluate(() => {
    const s = window.h.state;
    return {
      me: [...s.collaborators.values()].find((c) => c.isCurrentUser)?.id,
      directory: s.collaboratorDirectory
        ? [...s.collaboratorDirectory.keys()]
        : null,
      hidden: [...s.hiddenCollaboratorIds],
      locked: [...s.lockedCollaboratorIds],
      layering: s.collaboratorLayeringEnabled,
      order: s.collaboratorLayerOrder,
      newcomerDefault: s.newCollaboratorDefault,
      viewMode: s.viewModeEnabled,
    };
  });

const waitForApp = async (page) => {
  await page.waitForFunction(
    () => window.h && window.h.state && !window.h.state.isLoading,
    { timeout: 30000 },
  );
  await page.waitForFunction(
    () =>
      window.collab &&
      window.collab.portal &&
      window.collab.portal.socketInitialized,
    { timeout: 30000 },
  );
};

(async () => {
  const a = await launch("a");
  const b = await launch("b");
  try {
    const pa = await a.newPage();
    const errorsA = [];
    pa.on("pageerror", (e) => errorsA.push(String(e)));
    await pa.goto(URL);
    await waitForApp(pa);
    const aId = (await state(pa)).me;
    log("A joined as", aId, "default =", (await state(pa)).newcomerDefault);

    // layering on before the newcomer arrives
    await pa.evaluate(() => {
      const am = window.h.app.actionManager;
      am.executeAction(am.actions.toggleCollaboratorLayering, "ui");
    });

    const pb = await b.newPage();
    await pb.goto(URL);
    await waitForApp(pb);
    const bId = (await state(pb)).me;
    log("B (newcomer) joined as", bId);

    await pa.waitForFunction(
      (id) => window.h.state.collaboratorDirectory?.has(id),
      { timeout: 15000 },
      bId,
    );
    let sa = await state(pa);
    log(
      "A sees B: locked =",
      sa.locked.includes(bId),
      "hidden =",
      sa.hidden.includes(bId),
    );
    log("A layer order:", JSON.stringify(sa.order), "(me =", aId, ")");

    // B draws a rectangle
    await pb.keyboard.press("r");
    await pb.mouse.move(400, 300);
    await pb.mouse.down();
    await pb.mouse.move(600, 450, { steps: 5 });
    await pb.mouse.up();
    await pa.waitForFunction(() => window.h.elements.length > 0, {
      timeout: 15000,
    });
    log(
      "A received B's element:",
      (
        await pa.evaluate(() =>
          window.h.elements.map((e) => e.customData?.creatorId),
        )
      ).join(","),
    );

    // dropdown screenshot
    await pa.click("[data-testid='collaborator-visibility-trigger']");
    await sleep(500);
    await pa.screenshot({ path: path.join(OUT, "83-dropdown.png") });
    const radios = await pa.$$eval(
      "input[name='collaborator-newcomer-default']",
      (els) => els.map((e) => e.checked),
    );
    log(
      "dropdown radios (Visible, Locked, Hidden) checked:",
      JSON.stringify(radios),
    );
    // choose Visible in the UI
    const choices = await pa.$$(
      ".CollaboratorVisibilityMenu__newcomers .RadioGroup__choice input",
    );
    await choices[0].click();
    await sleep(300);
    log("after clicking Visible, default =", (await state(pa)).newcomerDefault);
    await pa.keyboard.press("Escape");

    // Export image with layering on and a newcomer present
    await pa.evaluate(() =>
      window.h.setState({ openDialog: { name: "imageExport" } }),
    );
    await sleep(2000);
    const t0 = Date.now();
    const responsive = await Promise.race([
      pa.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector(".ImageExportModal")),
      sleep(5000).then(() => "TIMEOUT"),
    ]);
    log(
      "Export dialog open, page responsive:",
      responsive,
      `(${Date.now() - t0}ms)`,
    );
    const preview = await pa.evaluate(() => {
      const c = document.querySelector(".ImageExportModal__preview canvas");
      return c ? `${c.width}x${c.height}` : null;
    });
    log("Export preview canvas:", preview);
    await pa.screenshot({ path: path.join(OUT, "83-export.png") });
    await pa.evaluate(() => window.h.setState({ openDialog: null }));

    // hide B and hide myself, then reload A
    await pa.evaluate(
      (ids) => {
        const am = window.h.app.actionManager;
        for (const id of ids) {
          am.executeAction(am.actions.toggleCollaboratorVisibility, "ui", id);
        }
      },
      [bId, aId],
    );
    sa = await state(pa);
    log(
      "before reload: hidden =",
      JSON.stringify(sa.hidden),
      "viewMode =",
      sa.viewMode,
      "layering =",
      sa.layering,
    );

    await pa.reload();
    await waitForApp(pa);
    await sleep(1000);
    sa = await state(pa);
    log("after reload: me =", sa.me, "(same:", sa.me === aId + ")");
    log(
      "after reload: default =",
      sa.newcomerDefault,
      "| hidden =",
      JSON.stringify(sa.hidden),
      "| locked =",
      JSON.stringify(sa.locked),
    );
    log(
      "after reload: layering =",
      sa.layering,
      "| order =",
      JSON.stringify(sa.order),
      "| viewMode =",
      sa.viewMode,
    );

    // a third person (new to A) joins: Visible was chosen → not locked
    const c = await launch("c");
    try {
      const pc = await c.newPage();
      await pc.goto(URL);
      await waitForApp(pc);
      const cId = (await state(pc)).me;
      await pa.waitForFunction(
        (id) => window.h.state.collaboratorDirectory?.has(id),
        { timeout: 15000 },
        cId,
      );
      sa = await state(pa);
      log(
        "third browser C joined as",
        cId,
        "→ A: locked =",
        sa.locked.includes(cId),
        "hidden =",
        sa.hidden.includes(cId),
      );
      log("A layer order now:", JSON.stringify(sa.order));
    } finally {
      await c.close();
    }

    log("page errors in A:", errorsA.length ? errorsA : "none");
  } finally {
    await a.close();
    await b.close();
  }
})().catch((e) => {
  console.error("FAILED:", e);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 21:35:31Z)**_

Phase 5 is done and committed as `70560039`: the "New collaborators" setting is in the dropdown. It works in a real two- and three-browser session in Edge, and Export image doesn't freeze with layering on and a newcomer present.

## What changed

- **The setting:** a "New collaborators" row with **Visible / Locked / Hidden**, directly below the Layering row.
  - It uses the existing `RadioGroup` pill control.
  - Desktop and the phone main menu render the same component, so it's in both.
  - Each option has a tooltip, e.g. "New collaborators start visible but locked".
- **Action:** `setNewCollaboratorDefault` sits next to the existing collaborator actions in `actionCollaboratorVisibility.ts`. It uses `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` and ignores unknown values. It reuses the options list from Phase 3.
- **Text:** a new `collaboratorNewcomer` block in `en.json`.

## Tests

**Dropdown tests, editor level** (new `collaboratorNewcomer.test.tsx`, 8 tests):

- A: the row is present with Visible, Locked, Hidden in that order.
- A: Locked is selected by default.
- A: choosing each of the three options selects it. Each test starts from a different option, so the click is a real change.
- C: choosing options doesn't touch anyone already seen. The hidden and locked sets stay the very same objects.
- G: choosing adds no undo entries.
- Phone: the setting is in the main menu's collaborator section and choosing an option works.

**App tests** (2 added to `collabNewcomer.test.tsx`):

- F: an option chosen in the dropdown is still selected after a reload, and the next newcomer gets it.
- Export image with layering on and a newcomer present: the preview renders, nothing errors, and the order is Miscellaneous, then the newcomer above it. Under #82's old rule the newcomer would have been drawn below Miscellaneous.

## Real-browser check

I ran the local room server and the app, then drove three separate Edge profiles with Puppeteer (A = me, B = newcomer, C = a later newcomer):

- A starts with Locked. B arrives locked and not hidden, and lands in A's order as `[A, B, Miscellaneous]`.
- In the dropdown, Locked is checked by default and clicking Visible selects it.
- Export image with layering on and B present: the dialog opens, the page responds in 2 ms, the preview renders, and there are no page errors.
- I hid B and myself (which turns on view mode) and reloaded A. Afterwards:
  - A has the same client id;
  - the default is Visible;
  - B is hidden and locked;
  - layering is on with the same order;
  - my own hide was **not** restored, so view mode is off.
- C then joined: unlocked (because the default is Visible), and placed directly above Miscellaneous.
- From the screenshot: the row fits the popover, with the pills on the right. The "New collaborators" label wraps onto two lines in the narrow popover; I left it, but say if you'd rather it stay on one line.

## Test results

- **Full suite:** `Tests 3 failed | 2720 passed | 47 skipped`. The 3 are the known Windows `exportToSvg` snapshots.
- **Type check and lint:** `tsc` exits 0. ESLint and Prettier are clean on the changed files. ESLint flagged one import-order warning, which I auto-fixed.
- **Intermittent cold-start failures:** some batch runs had 0–6 failures, all at `render`'s 1-second "still loading" wait.
  - The Phase 4 commit also failed 1 when I reran the batch, and the count varied from run to run on the same code.
  - Part of the cause: stopping the background servers only ended their shells, so the dev server and the room server kept running until I stopped them by process id.
  - With them stopped, the full suite passed apart from the 3 Windows snapshots.

## For your manual test

1. **Start the servers:** run the room server with `cd excalidraw-room && yarn start:dev` (port 3002) and the app with `yarn start` from the repo root (port 3001).
2. **Browser A** (e.g. Edge): open `http://localhost:3001` and start a live session from the share button. Open the `⋯` dropdown: "New collaborators" shows **Locked** selected.
3. **Browser B**, a different browser or a private window so it has separate storage: open the room link.
   - In A, B appears as visible but **locked**: their lock icon is on, you can see their drawings, and you can't select them.
4. **Layering:** in A, turn **Layering** on and have B draw something.
   - In A's dropdown, B's row sits directly **above "Untagged & unknown"**.
   - Now move "Untagged & unknown" up with ↑. When the next newcomer joins (step 9), they should go to the very bottom instead.
5. **Export:** in A, open **Export image** with layering on. The preview appears and the page doesn't freeze. Close it.
6. **Change the setting:** in A, select **Hidden**. B is unchanged (Criteria C).
7. **Hide yourself:** in A, hide your own row. The editor switches to view mode.
8. **Reload A** (accept the "leave page" prompt if it appears). After the reload:
   - Hidden is still selected;
   - B is still locked;
   - layering and the order are as you left them;
   - you're **not** hidden, and **not** in view mode.
9. **Browser C**, a third separate browser or profile: open the room link. In A, C arrives **hidden**, and in the layer order they're placed per steps 4 and 8.
10. **B leaves and rejoins:** close B and reopen the link. B keeps whatever you set for them; the newcomer default doesn't apply again.
11. **Another room:** in A, start a different room. It opens with nobody hidden or locked and layering off, but the "New collaborators" choice is still Hidden.
12. **Phone layout:** with device emulation, open the main menu, then the `⋯` in the collaborator section. The same setting is there.
13. **Dark mode:** toggle it and check the pills are readable.

**Tech debt**

- _Introduced:_
  - The settings module and the directory share the room-pruning helpers.
  - An older stored version is dropped on the next save; there's no migration.
  - `collabNewcomer.test.tsx` copies the socket, encryption and Firebase mocks, because `vi.mock` only works per file.
  - The typed `appState` variable in `updateCollaborator` works around `updateScene`'s key inference.
  - The Export dialog check in the app test copies about 30 lines from #82's dialog test.
- _Encountered:_
  - The directory reloads newest-first.
  - #116's pruning keeps the older room when two saves land in the same millisecond.
  - App tests time out at the first test of a file when the machine is busy.
  - Stopping a background server on Windows leaves the real server running.
  - The repo's Prettier version can't parse `satisfies`.
  - Puppeteer's default screenshot closes Radix popovers.

**DECISIONS LOG**

1. Plan: I proposed a newcomer check in `recordSighting` and separate helpers. You asked for no bloat and reuse of #81–84, so the check went in `updateCollaborator` and the logic is built from existing helpers.
2. Q1: I proposed placing newcomers literally directly above Miscellaneous, even when it's been moved up. You first agreed, then revised it: if Miscellaneous was moved up, newcomers go to the bottom (`f0823ed6`).
3. Q2: should my own new id be treated as a newcomer or go on top? You chose on top, then said "stick with what was before", which I've kept as on top.
4. Q3: I asked whether to leave or retitle the "resets on reload" tests. You said they're wrong because these settings persist and reset only on Reset, so they're retitled.
5. Q4: should a pruned collaborator who returns get the newcomer default? Yes; it replaces leftover saved state.
6. Shared room pruning: I recommended extracting it rather than copying it. You approved extracting.
7. Test 14: I offered a `version: 0` check. You wanted it as a fallback next to "version − 1".
8. Tests 8 and 19 (no-mutation checks): I offered to rename them. You kept them as backup coverage.
9. Checkpoints: I asked whether "approved going forward" meant I could run through the remaining phases. You said stop at every phase.
10. Phase 4: you approved it as matching the requirements and said you'd test manually and add test cases after Phase 5.

**Files changed** (`70560039`): `actionCollaboratorVisibility.ts`, `actions/index.ts`, `actions/types.ts`, `CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.tsx`, `CollaboratorVisibilityMenu.scss`, `locales/en.json`, `collaboratorNewcomer.test.tsx` (new), `collabNewcomer.test.tsx`.

I'll wait for your manual test results and the extra test cases before Phase 6 (full check and the `pr-83.md` draft).

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 21:52:57Z)**_

There are three causes. Two are environmental and unrelated to #83; the third is **a bug in my own test helper**, and I found it with diagnostics rather than inferring it.

**1. Three `exportToSvg` snapshots: a Windows-only path bug, already proven.**

- `setupTests.ts` builds the font path as `file://${__dirname}/`. On Windows, Vite turns that into `file:///c:/…/@fs/C:/…`, the font can't be found, and the SVG keeps font URLs instead of embedded fonts, so the snapshots don't match.
- It fails on `master` too and passes in CI (Linux). We proved this during #82 by temporarily patching the font loader.

**2. Intermittent "still loading" failures: this machine's speed, not the code.**

- The test helper `render` waits only 1 second for the app to finish loading. When many test files start at once, the first test in a file sometimes takes longer, which is why unrelated files like `LanguageList` and `MobileMenu` failed.
- **Proof:** I temporarily raised that wait to 10 seconds and reran `packages/element/tests` plus `excalidraw-app/tests`. About 15–20 failures dropped to 0 in one run and 1 in the other, and that 1 is cause 3. The commit before #83 shows the same failures. I reverted the change.
- **It got worse during Phase 5:** stopping my background servers only ended their shells, so the dev server and the room server kept running until I killed them by process id.

**3. The real one: my reload helper in `collabNewcomer.test.tsx` has a race.** It fails roughly 1 run in 5–10.

- **What happens:** every test first renders the app in `beforeEach`. My `openRoomLink` helper (used by the reload tests) then unmounts that app and puts a room link in the URL. But the unmounted app is still finishing its own start-up. It reads the new URL, its Collab joins the room, and it registers its socket handlers in the shared mock. The test then sends "first-in-room" to that **leftover** Collab. The app actually under test never receives it and never finishes joining, so the wait times out.
- **Proof from the trace of a failing run:** "open socket#31 by the beforeEach app's Collab (unmounted)", then "test calls first-in-room of socket#31", and only then "open socket#32 by the newly rendered app's Collab".
- **This isn't a product bug.** A real reload destroys the old page, so nothing is left behind, and the three-browser Edge run worked.
- **I was wrong in Phase 4.** I called this failure "slow under load" and raised a timeout. That hid it, but didn't fix it.

**Proposed fix (test code only):** give each mock socket its own handler map and message list, and have the helpers talk only to the socket of the app under test (`window.collab.portal.socket`). A leftover Collab can then neither receive the test's events nor pollute the "sends nothing" checks. I'd verify it by running the file 30 times in a row. The other collab test files never re-render the app, so they aren't affected.

I've reverted all temporary diagnostics, so the working tree matches commit `70560039`. Should I apply the fix now as a separate commit, or after your manual testing?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 22:20:05Z)**_

The race in my reload tests is fixed and committed as `5d1e0216`: the test file passed **30 runs out of 30**, where it used to fail about 1 run in 5–10. As you asked, I left the machine-speed timeouts alone.

**I had the cause partly wrong last time.** The old app wasn't finishing its start-up on its own. The app's Collab API is kept in a **global store** that isn't cleared when the app is unmounted. So when the test rendered the new app (to simulate a reload), the new app's start-up code first called the **old, unmounted app's Collab**, and that joined the room on its own socket. The test then talked to the wrong socket, which explains both symptoms:

- the app under test sometimes never finished joining the room;
- the room's stored scene sometimes never arrived. This one only appeared after I'd fixed the first part (1 run in 30).

**The fix, all in [collabNewcomer.test.tsx](excalidraw-app/tests/collabNewcomer.test.tsx). App code is unchanged:**

- The reload helper (`openRoomLink`) now clears that store before rendering the new app, as a real page reload does, and waits for the new app's Collab before joining.
- Each fake socket now keeps its own handlers and sent messages, and the helpers only use the socket of the app under test. If a leftover Collab ever opens a socket again, the tests can't reach it by mistake and it can't affect the "sends nothing" checks.

**Results:**

- Type check passes and ESLint is clean.
- Full suite: 2719 passed, 4 failed:
  - the 3 known Windows-only `exportToSvg` snapshots;
  - one `MermaidToExcalidraw` test, in a file #83 doesn't touch, which passes 2/2 on its own (the machine-speed kind).

**This isn't a product bug:** a real reload clears the store, and the three-browser Edge run worked. I'll list the store not being cleared on unmount under "Encountered" tech debt in the PR, since it affects any test that re-renders the app.

**DECISIONS LOG** 11. Test failures: I reported three causes and proposed patching only my test helper. You said to fix them because they're chronic, and that machine-speed timeouts are fine to ignore. I fixed the real cause and confirmed it with 30 consecutive passing runs (`5d1e0216`).

Ready for your manual test. Afterwards I'll add your extra test cases, then Phase 6.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 23:40:28Z)**_

Glad the rest works. The persistence trouble you hit within one browser is very likely by design, not a bug. Everything this feature saves is **per browser profile**, the same as #116's directory:

- Two tabs of the same browser have different client ids, but they share the saved settings for a room and the global default. The last tab to change something overwrites what's saved for that room.
- The collaborator directory is shared too. Someone first seen in one tab counts as "already seen" when another tab of that browser reloads, so they won't get the newcomer default there.

Testing with separate browsers or profiles (Edge + Chrome, or a private window) avoids this. I'll list it in the PR under "Not tested automatically" and Tech Debt as a known limitation, and I don't think it needs a change before Phase 6.

Starting Phase 6. The full suite with coverage takes a while, so I'll run it in the background and gather the PR material meanwhile:

```markdown
Closes #83 (Sub-issue of #14)

**Builds on #180 (#82, not merged yet):** this branch starts from `feat/issue-82-user-priority-and-layering`, so until #180 merges this PR's diff also shows #82's commits. The #83 commits are `0897ac2e`, `f0823ed6`, `71ddae90`, `70560039` and `5d1e0216`.

## Why

In a busy or open room, a new collaborator is fully interactive on my screen the moment they join, so their drawings can be selected or moved by accident before I notice them. And every choice I make in the collaborator dropdown (who's hidden, who's locked, layering and its order) is lost on reload, so I have to set the room up again each session.

This PR follows the [Design comment on #83](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/83):

- **New collaborators** setting (**Visible / Locked / Hidden**, default **Locked**), applied the first time this client sees someone;
- newcomers placed **directly above "unknown / miscellaneous"** in #82's layer order;
- the dropdown's settings are **saved locally**: the newcomer default for all rooms, and hidden, locked, the Layering switch and the order per room.

As with the rest of #14, everything stays on my device. Nothing reaches the shared scene, exports, other collaborators or undo history.

It builds on:

- **#116:** the collaborator directory ("seen before" = in the directory) and its per-room storage;
- **#81:** locking (hidden → also locked);
- **#82 (#180):** the layer order. Criteria D replaces #82's Criteria H ("newcomers go to the bottom").

## What changed

- **One pure rule.** `getNewcomerState` (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`) gives the state a first-seen collaborator starts in, built on #81's `addLockedCollaborators`. It never applies to me or to miscellaneous. #82's `getCollaboratorLayerOrder` now places newcomers directly above miscellaneous while it's the bottom row, otherwise at the very bottom; my own new client id goes on top.
- **Applied in one place.** `Collab.updateCollaborator` checks "not in the directory yet" before recording the sighting and merges the result into its existing `updateScene`. `recordSighting` is unchanged.
- **One small persistence module.** `excalidraw-app/collab/collaboratorSettings.ts`: one versioned localStorage entry next to #116's directory, sharing its room pruning (20 rooms). Sets are stored as arrays; anything unreadable, unknown or from another version falls back to the defaults. Hiding my own drawings is never saved or restored.
- **Restore and save.** Restored when a room starts and right after each scene reset on join (`resetScene` resets all of appState); saved from the app's `onChange` only when a setting changed. This also stops lock and layering state leaking into the next room.
- **State and UI.** `AppState.newCollaboratorDefault` (never persisted with the scene, exported or synced), a `setNewCollaboratorDefault` action (no history), and a Visible / Locked / Hidden row in the dropdown below Layering, using the existing `RadioGroup`, on desktop and phone.
- **Snapshots:** AppState snapshots gain the new field (133 added lines, nothing else).

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- **Shared room pruning.** The settings module reuses the directory's `readStoredObject` / `withRecentRooms`, so a change to one affects the other.
- **No migration.** Saved settings from another version are ignored and replaced on the next save.
- **One browser profile = one set of saved settings.** Tabs of the same browser share a room's saved settings (last change wins) and the directory, so a collaborator first seen in one tab isn't new in another.
- **Duplicated test mocks** in `collabNewcomer.test.tsx` (socket, encryption, Firebase), as in #81/#82 (`vi.mock` is per file).
- **A typed variable in `updateCollaborator`** works around `updateScene` inferring its keys from the object literal.

**Encountered:**

- **`resetScene` resets all of appState** when joining a room; #116 republishes the directory afterwards, and this PR restores the saved settings the same way.
- **The Collab API lives in a global jotai store** that unmounting doesn't clear. Tests that re-render the app must reset it, or the new app drives the old Collab (fixed in `5d1e0216` after it made reload tests flaky).
- **#116's room pruning keeps the older room** when two saves land in the same millisecond.
- **Join order after a reload** comes from the directory, which loads newest-first (accepted in #82).
- **Windows-only test setup bug:** 3 `exportToSvg` snapshots fail locally on Windows (on `master` too); CI is unaffected. On a busy machine, the first test of some files can also time out while the app loads.
```

```text
142	const getSentUpdates = () =>
143	  (getSocket()?.emitted ?? [])
144	    .filter(([event]) => event === WS_EVENTS.SERVER)
145	    .map(([, , buffer]) => JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(buffer)))
146	    .filter(
147	      (message) =>
148	        message.type === WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE ||
149	        message.type === WS_SUBTYPES.INIT,
150	    );
151
152	/** simulates a message from another client arriving through the room */
153	const deliver = async (
154	  message: SocketUpdateDataSource[keyof SocketUpdateDataSource],
155	) => {
156	  await getHandler("client-broadcast")(
157	    new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(message)),
158	    new Uint8Array(12),
159	  );
160	};
161
162	/** local changes reach Collab through onChange → syncElements */
163	const sync = () => {
164	  act(() => {
165	    window.collab.syncElements(h.app.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted());
166	  });
167	};
168
169	const execute = (name: string, value?: unknown) => {
170	  const action = h.app.actionManager.actions[name as ActionName];
171	  assert.isDefined(action, `action "${name}" should be registered`);
172	  act(() => {
173	    h.app.actionManager.executeAction(action, "ui", value as any);
174	  });
175	};
176
177	const getClientId = () => window.collab.getClientId()!;
178
179	/** the server's member list (it always includes me, "my-socket") */
180	const roomMembersAre = async (...socketIds: string[]) => {
181	  act(() => {
182	    getHandler("room-user-change")(["my-socket", ...socketIds]);
183	  });
184	};
185
186	/**
187	 * what the server does when we join: we're alone ("first-in-room"), and the
188	 * member list (which tells the editor which collaborator is me)
189	 */
190	const finishInitialization = async () => {
191	  // opening a room link joins asynchronously (client id, socket.io import),
192	  // which can take over waitFor's 1s default when the machine is busy
193	  await waitFor(
194	    () => expect(getSocket()?.handlers.has("first-in-room")).toBe(true),
195	    { timeout: 5000 },
196	  );
197	  await getHandler("first-in-room")();
198	  await waitFor(() =>
199	    expect(window.collab.portal.socketInitialized).toBe(true),
200	  );
201	  await roomMembersAre();
202	};
203
204	/** start a new room and finish initialization (we're alone in it) */
205	const startNewRoom = async () => {
206	  act(() => {
207	    window.collab.startCollaboration(null);
208	  });
209	  await finishInitialization();
210	};
211
212	/** join an existing room (as from a room link) and finish initialization */
213	const joinRoom = async (room: { roomId: string; roomKey: string }) => {
214	  act(() => {
215	    window.collab.startCollaboration(room);
216	  });
217	  await finishInitialization();
218	};
219
220	/**
221	 * Opens the app on the room's link, like loading or reloading the page
222	 * (the app joins the room by itself), and waits until the scene is loaded.
223	 * Storage (local and session) is kept, like in a real reload.
224	 */
225	const openRoomLink = async (room: { roomId: string; roomKey: string }) => {
226	  const previousCollab = window.collab;
227	  unmountComponent();
228	  // a real reload starts with fresh module state. The app's Collab API lives
229	  // in a global store that unmounting doesn't clear, so without this the new
230	  // app would first start collaborating through the unmounted app's Collab
231	  appJotaiStore.set(collabAPIAtom, null);
232	  window.history.replaceState(
233	    {},
234	    "",
235	    `${window.location.origin}/#room=${room.roomId},${room.roomKey}`,
236	  );
237	  // the app keeps loading until the room is initialized, and `render` waits
238	  // for loading to finish, so initialize the room while it renders
239	  const rendering = render(<ExcalidrawApp />);
240	  // until the new app's Collab mounts, `window.collab` is still the old one
241	  await waitFor(() => expect(window.collab).not.toBe(previousCollab), {
242	    timeout: 5000,
243	  });
244	  await finishInitialization();
245	  await rendering;
246	};
247
248	/** a peer introduces themselves (#116's USER_IDENTITY) */
249	const peerJoins = async (clientId: string, socketId = `${clientId}-socket`) => {
250	  await deliver({
251	    type: WS_SUBTYPES.USER_IDENTITY,
252	    payload: {
253	      socketId: socketId as SocketId,
254	      clientId,
255	      username: clientId,
256	    },
257	  });
258	  await waitFor(() =>
259	    expect(h.state.collaboratorDirectory?.has(clientId)).toBe(true),
260	  );
261	};
262
263	const isHidden = (id: string) => h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has(id);
264	const isLocked = (id: string) => h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds.has(id);
265
266	/** what AC-H says must not change */
267	const getShared = () =>
268	  h.elements.map(({ id, index, version, versionNonce }) => ({
269	    id,
270	    index,
271	    version,
272	    versionNonce,
273	  }));
274
275	/** a peer's element arrives in the room */
276	const receivePeerElement = async (id: string, creatorId: string) => {
277	  await deliver({
278	    type: WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE,
279	    payload: {
280	      elements: syncInvalidIndices([
281	        ...h.app.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted(),
282	        stamp(API.createElement({ id }), creatorId),
283	      ]),
284	    },
285	  });
286	  await waitFor(() =>
287	    expect(h.elements.some((element) => element.id === id)).toBe(true),
288	  );
289	};
290
291	beforeEach(async () => {
292	  mocks.storedRoomElements = null;
293	  localStorage.clear();
294	  sessionStorage.clear();
295	  // a previous test's room link would make the app auto-join that room
296	  window.history.replaceState({}, "", window.location.origin);
297	  await render(<ExcalidrawApp />);
298	});
299
300	afterEach(() => {
301	  vi.restoreAllMocks();
302	});
```

Below is the flow summary at both levels, then a line-by-line walkthrough of the tests you haven't reviewed yet: the app-level file (26 tests) and the dropdown file (8 tests), plus the small edits to #81/#82 tests since your Phase 2 review.

---

# Part 1: How it works

## A. Excalidraw architecture: where each piece lives and why

Excalidraw is split into layers. #83 puts each piece in the layer that already owns that kind of job, and adds no new kind of plumbing.

```
packages/element      → pure rules, no React, no storage
   ownership.ts         getNewcomerState, getCollaboratorLayerOrder (#82, changed)
        ▲ used by
packages/excalidraw   → the editor component (published to npm)
   appState.ts/types    newCollaboratorDefault (browser/export/server: false)
   actions/             setNewCollaboratorDefault (CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER)
   components/          "New collaborators" row in the dropdown (RadioGroup)
        ▲ hosted by
excalidraw-app        → the website: collaboration + storage
   collab/Collab.tsx    applies the default, restores and saves settings
   collab/collaboratorSettings.ts   localStorage, one versioned entry
   App.tsx onChange     hands each AppState to Collab to save
```

The design choices, and the existing Excalidraw patterns they follow:

1. **Pure rules sit in `packages/element`.** #116, #81 and #82 already put their rules in `ownership.ts`: visibility, locking and layer order. The newcomer rule goes there too and is built from #81's `addLockedCollaborators`. Pure code is easy to unit-test and to mutation-test with Stryker.
2. **AppState holds the live values; the host app owns saving them.** The editor package is a library that knows nothing about rooms. Rooms, the directory and sockets live in `excalidraw-app`. That's why #116's directory is saved by the app, not the editor, and #83's settings follow the same pattern. The AppState fields stay `browser/export/server: false`, so Excalidraw's own scene save, file export and room sync never see them. Only our module saves them, per room.
3. **"Local only" uses the mechanisms Excalidraw already has:**
   - Actions return `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER`, so nothing enters undo/redo history.
   - Collab calls `updateScene` with _only_ `appState`, so no element changes. Collab sends the scene to the room only when element versions change, so nothing is sent.
4. **No new rendering or hit-testing code.** Once a newcomer is in `hiddenCollaboratorIds` or `lockedCollaboratorIds`, the existing #116 and #81 checks hide them or block them. Their place in the layer order is drawn by #82's single ordering function, which the canvas, clicking and export all use. That's why "Export image doesn't freeze" only needed checking, not new code.
5. **The join quirk.** When joining a room, Excalidraw's `resetScene()` replaces all of AppState with defaults. #116 already handled this by republishing the directory. #83 restores the saved settings at that same moment.

## B. The feature, step by step

**1. Opening a room** (`Collab.startCollaboration`)

- #116 loads the room's directory. In the same `updateScene` call, `loadRoomSettings(roomId)` reads `collaboratorSettings.ts`, which gives back:
  - the newcomer default (global);
  - hidden, locked, layering and order for this room, with Sets rebuilt from arrays;
  - my own id removed from the hidden list.
- `settingsRoomId = roomId` marks the settings as "in the editor"; saving is allowed from then on.

**2. Joining an existing room resets the scene** (`resetSceneKeepingSettings`)

- `settingsRoomId = null` blocks saving, so the defaults about to appear can't overwrite the saved settings.
- `resetScene()` resets everything, and on the next line `loadRoomSettings` puts the room's settings back.

**3. A peer appears** (`Collab.updateCollaborator`, called for identity, pointer and idle messages)

- Cheap check first: does the message carry an id, are we in a room, and is the id **not** in the directory yet?
- If it's new, `getNewcomerState(id, current state + the directory before this sighting)` decides the result:
  - me, Miscellaneous, or anyone in the directory → `null` (no change);
  - Locked → added to the lock set;
  - Hidden → added to the hidden set and the lock set;
  - Visible → removed from both (clears leftovers);
  - if a layer order exists, the newcomer goes directly above Miscellaneous while it's the bottom row, otherwise to the very bottom.
- Then `recordSighting` runs, unchanged, so next time they're "seen before".
- The result goes into the **same** `updateScene` that already publishes collaborators, so there's no extra render.

**4. The editor reacts on its own.** The renderer, hit-testing and the dropdown rows read the new sets and order through the #116, #81 and #82 code.

**5. You change something in the dropdown** (Hide, Lock, Layering, move a row, or the new radio buttons)

- An action updates AppState with `NEVER`.
- The app's `onChange` calls `collabAPI.saveCollaboratorSettings(appState)`.
- That compares the five settings **by reference** with the last saved ones. If nothing changed, it returns right away; this runs on every editor change, so it has to be cheap. If something changed, it writes to localStorage.

**6. A reload** repeats step 1. Settings come back and hiding my own drawings doesn't, so #116's "force view mode while my drawings are hidden" rule doesn't fire.

**7. Leaving the room** clears `settingsRoomId`, so solo work after a session never writes into the room's entry.

---

# Part 2: Test walkthrough

## `excalidraw-app/tests/collabNewcomer.test.tsx` (26 tests)

This file runs the **real** app (`ExcalidrawApp`), the real `Collab` and the real `Portal`. Only the network edge is faked.

### The fakes

```ts
vi.mock("socket.io-client", () => ({ default: () => { const handlers = new Map(); const emitted = []; return { id: "my-socket", handlers, emitted, on: (event, handler) => handlers.set(event, handler), emit: (...args) => emitted.push(args), ... }; } }));
```

- Each time the app creates a socket, it gets a fresh fake.
- `on(...)` stores the app's handler for a server event, e.g. "first-in-room". The test calls it later to play the server.
- `emit(...)` records what the app sends, so tests can check "nothing was sent".
- Each socket keeps its _own_ handlers and messages. This is the race fix from `5d1e0216`.
- `id: "my-socket"` is this client's socket id.

```ts
vi.mock("@excalidraw/excalidraw/data/encryption", ...)
```

- Encryption passes data through unchanged, so tests can read sent messages as JSON.

```ts
vi.mock("../data/firebase", () => ({ loadFromFirebase: async () => mocks.storedRoomElements, ... }))
```

- The room's stored scene is whatever the test puts in `mocks.storedRoomElements`, so a test can make a room that already has a drawing in it.

### Helpers

```ts
const ROOM = { roomId: "room83", roomKey: "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv" };
```

- A room link. The key must be 22 characters, or the app rejects the link.

```ts
const getSocket = () => window.collab.portal.socket;
const getHandler = (event) => getSocket()!.handlers.get(event)!;
```

- `window.collab` is the Collab of the app being tested. Every server event the test plays goes to **its** socket only.

```ts
const getSentUpdates = () =>
  (getSocket()?.emitted ?? [])
    .filter(([event]) => event === WS_EVENTS.SERVER)
    .map(decode)
    .filter((m) => m.type === UPDATE || m.type === INIT);
```

- Scene messages this client sent: updates and full-scene inits. Identity and pointer messages aren't counted, since they never carry elements.

```ts
const deliver = async (message) => {
  await getHandler("client-broadcast")(encode(message), iv);
};
```

- Plays "a message from a peer arrives through the room".

```ts
const execute = (name, value) => { ...actionManager.executeAction(action, "ui", value) inside act() };
```

- Runs a real editor action, the same thing a dropdown click does. `act()` flushes React, so the state is final when the next line runs.

```ts
const roomMembersAre = async (...socketIds) => {
  getHandler("room-user-change")(["my-socket", ...socketIds]);
};
```

- Plays the server's member list. It always includes me, which is how the editor learns which collaborator is me (`isCurrentUser`). Without it, my id is unknown and Criteria E can't be tested.

```ts
const finishInitialization = async () => {
  await waitFor(
    () => expect(getSocket()?.handlers.has("first-in-room")).toBe(true),
    { timeout: 5000 },
  );
  await getHandler("first-in-room")();
  await waitFor(() =>
    expect(window.collab.portal.socketInitialized).toBe(true),
  );
  await roomMembersAre();
};
```

1. Wait until the app has opened its socket and is listening. Joining is async, so this gets 5 seconds on a busy machine.
2. Play "you're the first in the room". The app runs `initializeRoom`, which also resets the scene and restores settings when joining by link.
3. Wait until the room is fully initialized.
4. Play the member list.

```ts
const startNewRoom = async () => {
  act(() => {
    window.collab.startCollaboration(null);
  });
  await finishInitialization();
};
const joinRoom = async (room) => {
  act(() => {
    window.collab.startCollaboration(room);
  });
  await finishInitialization();
};
```

- `null` means "create a new room", like clicking Share. Passing a room means joining an existing room by its link; that path loads its saved settings and goes through the reset.

```ts
const openRoomLink = async (room) => {
  const previousCollab = window.collab;
  unmountComponent();
  appJotaiStore.set(collabAPIAtom, null);
  window.history.replaceState(
    {},
    "",
    `${origin}/#room=${room.roomId},${room.roomKey}`,
  );
  const rendering = render(<ExcalidrawApp />);
  await waitFor(() => expect(window.collab).not.toBe(previousCollab), {
    timeout: 5000,
  });
  await finishInitialization();
  await rendering;
};
```

This simulates **loading or reloading the page** on a room link:

1. Remember the old Collab, then throw the old app away.
2. Clear the global Collab-API store. A real reload starts with empty memory; without this, the new app would first drive the old Collab. That was the race.
3. Put the room link in the address bar.
4. Render a brand-new app. It reads the link and joins by itself, through the real page-load path.
5. Wait until the new app's Collab exists, then play the server.
6. Wait until loading finishes.

localStorage and sessionStorage are **not** cleared, exactly as in a real reload. So my client id and the saved settings survive.

```ts
const peerJoins = async (clientId, socketId = `${clientId}-socket`) => {
  await deliver({
    type: USER_IDENTITY,
    payload: { socketId, clientId, username: clientId },
  });
  await waitFor(() =>
    expect(h.state.collaboratorDirectory?.has(clientId)).toBe(true),
  );
};
```

- A peer announces themselves with #116's identity message, which is how a real newcomer appears.
- Then it waits until they're in the directory, i.e. Collab has processed them.

```ts
const isHidden = (id) => h.state.hiddenCollaboratorIds.has(id);
const isLocked = (id) => h.state.lockedCollaboratorIds.has(id);
```

- These read the editor's live state.

```ts
const getShared = () =>
  h.elements.map(({ id, index, version, versionNonce }) => ({
    id,
    index,
    version,
    versionNonce,
  }));
```

- The shared fields Criteria H says must not change. `versionNonce` is included because any edit changes it too.

```ts
const receivePeerElement = async (id, creatorId) => { await deliver({ type: UPDATE, payload: { elements: [...current, stamped element] } }); await waitFor(element present); };
```

- A peer's drawing arrives, stamped with its creator (#116's `creatorId`).

```ts
beforeEach: mocks.storedRoomElements = null;
localStorage.clear();
sessionStorage.clear();
replaceState(origin);
await render(<ExcalidrawApp />);
```

- Every test starts clean: no saved settings, no client id, no room link, and a fresh app.

---

### Criteria A and B

**1. `AC-A: in a room, the New collaborators setting starts as Locked`**

```ts
await startNewRoom();
expect(h.state.newCollaboratorDefault).toBe("locked");
```

- Storage is empty, so this is the true first-run default after the room's settings are loaded.
- **Source:** Criteria A, "defaults to Locked".

**2. `AC-B: by default, a collaborator joining for the first time starts visible but locked`**

```ts
await startNewRoom();
await peerJoins("alice");
expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);
```

- Alice is new to this client, so with the default she's visible but locked.
- This is the main end-to-end path: identity message → `updateCollaborator` → `getNewcomerState` → editor state.
- **Source:** Criteria B, "Locked → visible but locked".

**3. `AC-B: with Visible, … starts visible and interactive`**

```ts
await startNewRoom();
API.setAppState({ newCollaboratorDefault: "visible" });
await peerJoins("alice");
expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
```

- The default is changed _after_ the room starts. If set before, the room's restore would put back the saved value, Locked.
- On its own this would also pass if nothing happened, which is why Test 4 exists.

**4. `AC-B (decision Q4): with Visible, a first-time collaborator's leftover saved lock is cleared`**

```ts
saveCollaboratorSettings(
  ROOM.roomId,
  {
    newCollaboratorDefault: "visible",
    hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(),
    lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]),
    collaboratorLayeringEnabled: false,
    collaboratorLayerOrder: null,
  },
  null,
);
await joinRoom(ROOM);
expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(true);
await peerJoins("alice");
expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
```

- **Setup:** the room's saved settings say alice is locked, but she's not in the directory, as if she'd been pruned from it.
- **Line 3:** the restore worked, so alice is locked before she appears.
- **Line 4:** she appears and counts as first-seen, so Visible applies and **removes** the leftover lock.
- **Why it matters:** this proves Visible actively does something; with the app wiring removed it fails.
- **Source:** your Q4 decision.

**5. `AC-B: with Hidden, … starts hidden (and therefore locked)`**

- Same shape as Test 3, with Hidden: alice ends up in both sets.
- **Source:** Criteria B and #81's "hidden implies locked".

**6. `AC-B: a collaborator first seen through a pointer message starts in the default too`**

```ts
await deliver({ type: MOUSE_LOCATION, payload: { socketId: "bob-socket", pointer: {...}, button: "up", selectedElementIds: {}, username: "Bob", clientId: "bob" } });
await waitFor(() => expect(isLocked("bob")).toBe(true));
```

- Bob's first message is a cursor move, not an identity message. Older clients, or a message arriving out of order, can do this.
- All three message types go through `updateCollaborator`, and this proves the default applies however someone is first seen.

**7. `AC-B: a collaborator who leaves and rejoins keeps the settings I gave them`**

```ts
await startNewRoom();
await peerJoins("alice"); // locked by default
execute("toggleCollaboratorLock", "alice"); // I unlock her
expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
await roomMembersAre(); // member list without alice → she left
await peerJoins("alice", "alice-socket-2"); // she rejoins, new connection
expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
expect(isHidden("alice")).toBe(false);
```

- She rejoins with a **new socket** but the same client id, like a reconnect.
- She's in the directory, so the default must **not** re-lock her.
- **Source:** Criteria B, "seen before (… even if they left) is not affected when they rejoin".

```ts
);

await peerJoins("bob");
expect(isLocked("alice")).toBe(false);
expect(isLocked("bob")).toBe(true);
```

- **Setup:** #116's saved directory says this browser saw alice in this room on an earlier day.
- After joining, alice isn't new, so she isn't locked. Bob was never seen, so he is: that's the control in the same test.

Those two halves only agree while Miscellaneous is the bottom row. If you've moved Miscellaneous up, the code now puts the newcomer at the very bottom, _below_ Miscellaneous (`f0823ed6`). That keeps "below every collaborator" but breaks "directly above Miscellaneous". A reviewer checking D word for word would flag it, so it should be amended and approved on the issue, as you did with #81's Criteria E.

## Refinements to record (no AC change)

These fit the ACs but settle points they don't cover. On #82 you recorded these in an "implementation decisions" comment; doing the same here would let the PR cite them as **issue discussion** instead of "other".

1. **My own new client id goes on top** of a restored order (Q2). Criteria E covers the setting, not my place in the layer order.
2. **A collaborator pruned from #116's directory who returns gets the default again**, replacing their leftover saved state (Q4). This follows from Criteria B's definition of "new".
3. **A newcomer is written into the stored layer order even while layering is off**, so they're already above Miscellaneous when you turn it back on. Criteria D only says "while layering is on".
4. **Saving is per browser profile:** two tabs of one browser share a room's saved settings, and the last change wins. That fits "stays on this device", but a reviewer may ask.

**No action needed:**

- Restoring per room also stops lock and layering state carrying into the next room. That's exactly what Criteria F describes.

Written for: reviewers and teammates reading issue #83.

**Amended Criteria D** (to replace the current line in the issue body):

> - [ ] **Criteria D: Newcomers in the layer order.** While layering is on, a newcomer is added below every collaborator already in the order: directly above "unknown / miscellaneous" while it's the bottom row, or at the very bottom if I've moved it up. Several newcomers are added in join order. This replaces #82's Criteria H ("added to the bottom").

**Implementation decisions comment:**

> ## Implementation decisions
>
> Settled during implementation (PR to follow, building on #180):
>
> 1. **Miscellaneous moved up (Criteria D, amended above).** Newcomers go directly above "unknown / miscellaneous" while it's the bottom row. If I've moved it up, they go to the very bottom, so they're still below every collaborator already in the order.
> 2. **My own new client id** (e.g. a new tab) goes on top of a restored layer order, as in #82's default order. It isn't treated as a newcomer (Criteria E).
> 3. **Pruned collaborators.** Someone no longer in #116's directory counts as first-seen when they return (Criteria B), so they get the newcomer default, which replaces any leftover saved hidden/locked state.
> 4. **Layering off.** A newcomer is still placed in a stored layer order while layering is off, so turning it back on gives the Criteria D position.
> 5. **Per browser profile.** Settings are saved per browser profile, like #116's directory: tabs of the same browser share a room's saved settings (the last change wins).
